name: Flat Barbell Bench Press
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Lie flat on the bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Position your eyes directly under the barbell.
Grip the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart using a full overhand grip.
Retract and depress your shoulder blades, driving them into the bench.
Unrack the bar and hold it directly over your chest with locked elbows.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar slowly to your mid-chest, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45-degree angle.
Touch the bar lightly to your chest without bouncing it.
Exhale and push the bar back up in a slight diagonal arc toward your face.
Lock out your elbows at the top of the movement while keeping your shoulders retracted.
cues: Bend the bar with your hands to engage your lats.
Keep your feet rooted to the floor like tree roots.
Push yourself away from the bar into the bench.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees, which places excessive stress on the shoulders.
Bouncing the bar off the chest to gain momentum.
Lifting the hips and glutes off the bench during the lift.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
target: Clavicular Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest), Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Set an incline bench to an angle of approximately 30 to 45 degrees.
Lie back on the bench and plant your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the barbell with a medium-wide overhand grip.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back into the bench.
Unrack the barbell and stabilize it directly over your upper chest.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar under control to your upper chest (just below the collarbone).
Keep your elbows tucked at a 45-to-60-degree angle relative to your torso.
Pause briefly at the bottom without letting the bar rest on your chest.
Exhale and press the bar straight up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
cues: Drive your upper back hard into the bench.
Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.
Imagine pushing your body away from the weight.
mistakes: Using an excessively steep bench angle, which shifts the focus entirely to the front deltoids.
Bouncing the bar off the upper sternum or collarbone.
Allowing the wrists to bend backward under the weight.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
target: Costal Pectoralis Major (Lower Chest), Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Secure your legs under the pads of a decline bench set to roughly 15 to 30 degrees.
Lie back and ensure your head and upper back are fully supported.
Grip the bar with a medium-wide overhand grip.
Retract your shoulder blades and unrack the bar, holding it directly over your lower chest.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar slowly toward your lower chest or upper abdomen.
Keep your elbows tucked slightly, avoiding a complete 90-degree flare.
Touch the bar lightly to your lower chest.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position, locking out your elbows.
cues: Push the bar away from your lower chest.
Keep your shoulders pinned back throughout the movement.
Squeeze your chest at the top of the lift.
mistakes: Lowering the bar too high on the chest, which strains the shoulders.
Using an excessive decline angle that limits the range of motion.
Losing control of the bar on the descent due to the decline angle.

name: Flat Dumbbell Bench Press
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting on each knee.
Lie back on the bench while using your thighs to kick the dumbbells up to your chest.
Plant your feet flat on the floor and retract your shoulder blades.
Hold the dumbbells at the sides of your chest with your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
execution: Exhale and press the dumbbells straight up over your chest, bringing them close together but not touching.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Lower the weights until you feel a deep stretch in your chest.
Pause for a split second at the bottom before initiating the next press.
cues: Squeeze your armpits as you press up.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
Control the descent; don't let gravity drop the weights.
mistakes: Clashing the dumbbells together at the top, which loses tension on the chest.
Flaring the elbows out wide, putting the rotator cuffs at risk.
Failing to use a full range of motion at the bottom.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
target: Clavicular Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest), Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Set an incline bench to a 30-to-45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell on each knee.
Lie back and kick the dumbbells up to shoulder height one at a time.
Press your feet into the floor and pull your shoulders back and down.
execution: Exhale and press the dumbbells upward and slightly inward over your upper chest.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells under control to the sides of your upper chest.
Maintain a 45-to-60-degree elbow angle relative to your torso.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch in your upper pectorals, then press again.
cues: Press the weights up and together without letting them touch.
Keep your chest high and proud.
Drive through your feet to stabilize your body.
mistakes: Setting the bench angle too high, shifting the load to the shoulders.
Allowing the dumbbells to drift too far forward or backward during the press.
Shortening the range of motion by stopping the weights high above the chest.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
target: Costal Pectoralis Major (Lower Chest), Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Sit on a decline bench and secure your feet under the leg rollers.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
Lie back carefully, bringing the dumbbells to the sides of your lower chest.
Keep your shoulders retracted and pressed into the bench.
execution: Exhale and press the dumbbells straight up over your lower chest.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly, keeping your elbows tucked at a 45-degree angle.
Lower the weights until they are level with your chest, feeling a deep stretch.
Pause briefly, then press the dumbbells back to the starting position.
cues: Press the dumbbells away from your lower ribs.
Keep your wrists rigid and aligned with your forearms.
Focus on contracting the lower portion of your chest.
mistakes: Allowing the dumbbells to drift over your face, which is dangerous and incorrect.
Dropping the weights too quickly on the descent.
Using an excessive decline angle that causes discomfort or dizziness.

name: Flat Dumbbell Flyes
setup: Lie flat on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Press the dumbbells directly above your chest with palms facing each other.
Plant your feet flat on the floor and retract your shoulder blades.
Slightly bend your elbows and lock them in this position throughout the exercise.
execution: Inhale and lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc.
Keep the slight bend in your elbows constant; do not turn this into a press.
Lower the weights until your arms are parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and reverse the movement, hugging an imaginary large tree to bring the weights back up.
cues: Imagine hugging a giant barrel or tree.
Keep the elbow angle locked; don't let it bend more as you lower.
Squeeze your chest at the top of the movement.
mistakes: Bending the elbows too much, turning the fly into a press.
Lowering the weights too far, which overstretches and risks shoulder injury.
Clashing the dumbbells together at the top, losing muscle tension.

name: Incline Dumbbell Flyes
target: Clavicular Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest), Anterior Deltoids
setup: Set an incline bench to a 30-degree angle.
Lie back on the bench holding dumbbells directly above your upper chest.
Ensure your palms are facing each other and your feet are flat on the floor.
Maintain a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
execution: Inhale and lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide, controlled arc.
Maintain the fixed elbow angle as you lower the weights.
Stop when you feel a comfortable stretch across your upper chest.
Exhale and squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
cues: Lead the movement with your elbows.
Keep your chest puffed up toward the ceiling.
Focus on pulling your biceps toward each other at the top.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to bend completely, converting the fly into an incline press.
Lowering the weights past the plane of your torso, risking shoulder strain.
Using weights that are too heavy, leading to poor form and momentum.

name: Cable Crossover (High-to-Low)
target: Costal Pectoralis Major (Lower Chest), Sternal Pectoralis Major
setup: Set the pulleys on a cable crossover machine to the highest position.
Attach D-handles to both pulleys and grasp them with an overhand grip.
Step forward between the pulleys and take a staggered stance for stability.
Lean your torso slightly forward and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Exhale and sweep your arms downward and inward in a wide arc.
Bring your hands together in front of your hips, crossing one hand slightly over the other.
Inhale and slowly return your arms to the starting position, maintaining the elbow bend.
Control the weight all the way back until you feel a stretch in your chest.
cues: Sweep your hands down and together as if hugging someone.
Keep your core tight and do not swing your torso.
Squeeze your lower chest hard at the bottom of the movement.
mistakes: Using too much weight, causing the torso to swing or lean excessively.
Pressing the cables down instead of flying them in an arc.
Allowing the shoulders to roll forward at the end of the movement.

name: Low-to-High Cable Flyes
target: Clavicular Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest), Anterior Deltoids
setup: Set the pulleys on a cable machine to the lowest position.
Attach D-handles and hold them with your palms facing forward.
Step forward to create tension on the cables and adopt a staggered stance.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and a slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Exhale and sweep your arms upward and inward in a wide arc.
Bring your hands together in front of your upper chest or face level.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Maintain the slight bend in your elbows throughout the entire range of motion.
cues: Drive your biceps up and in toward your chin.
Keep your chest high and do not shrug your shoulders.
Control the stretch on the way down.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders, which shifts the work to the upper trapezius.
Bending the elbows too much and turning the movement into a biceps curl.
Leaning too far forward, which changes the angle of pull.

name: Chest Dips
target: Costal Pectoralis Major (Lower Chest), Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Grip the parallel bars of a dip station and press yourself up to lock your elbows.
Cross your ankles behind you and bend your knees slightly.
Lean your torso forward at roughly a 30-degree angle.
Pull your shoulders down and away from your ears.
execution: Inhale and lower your body slowly by bending your elbows.
Allow your elbows to flare out slightly to the sides to target the chest.
Lower yourself until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows, or until you feel a deep stretch.
Exhale and press back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest at the top.
cues: Keep your chin tucked and your torso leaned forward.
Flare your elbows slightly to keep the tension on your chest.
Imagine pushing the bars down away from you.
mistakes: Keeping the torso completely upright, which shifts the focus to the triceps.
Dropping down too fast, which can injure the shoulder joints.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears during the descent.

name: Push-Ups
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Get into a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Align your shoulders directly over your wrists.
Engage your core, glutes, and quads to form a straight line from head to heels.
Keep your gaze focused slightly in front of your hands.
execution: Inhale and lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked at a 45-degree angle.
Lower yourself until your chest is just an inch off the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Exhale and press through your palms to return to the starting high plank position.
cues: Keep your body as rigid as a wooden board.
Push the floor away from you.
Don't let your hips sag or your butt stick up.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees, placing stress on the shoulders.
Allowing the lower back to sag, which deactivates the core.
Doing partial reps and not lowering the chest close enough to the floor.

name: Incline Push-Ups
target: Costal Pectoralis Major (Lower Chest), Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart on an elevated surface (bench, box, or step).
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and glutes to stabilize your spine.
Keep your neck in a neutral position.
execution: Inhale and lower your chest slowly toward the elevated surface.
Keep your elbows tucked at a 45-degree angle relative to your torso.
Touch your chest lightly to the edge of the surface.
Exhale and press through your hands to return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your body in a straight line.
Push through the heels of your hands.
Squeeze your chest at the top.
mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of keeping the body straight.
Flaring the elbows out wide.
Using a surface that is unstable or slippery.

name: Decline Push-Ups
target: Clavicular Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest), Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Place your feet on an elevated surface (bench, box, or step).
Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Align your shoulders over your wrists and engage your core.
Ensure your body forms a straight line from head to toes.
execution: Inhale and lower your chest toward the floor under control.
Keep your elbows tucked at a 45-degree angle.
Lower until your chest is just above the floor.
Exhale and press through your hands to return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your core braced and hips elevated.
Push the floor away with force.
Control the descent; don't let your face drop first.
mistakes: Allowing the hips to sag, which hyperextends the lower back.
Flaring the elbows out to the sides.
Looking up or down too much, straining the neck.

name: Diamond Push-Ups
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Get into a high plank position.
Place your hands close together directly under your chest, forming a diamond shape with your index fingers and thumbs.
Engage your core, glutes, and legs to maintain a straight line.
Keep your head in a neutral position.
execution: Inhale and lower your chest slowly toward your hands.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides as you descend.
Lower until your chest touches or comes close to your hands.
Exhale and press through your palms to return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your elbows tucked tight to your ribs.
Squeeze your chest and triceps at the top.
Maintain a rock-solid core.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare out, which strains the elbows and shoulders.
Sagging at the hips or lower back.
Placing the hands too far forward instead of directly under the chest.

name: Pec Deck Flyes
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Clavicular Pectoralis Major
setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles are at chest level.
Sit back flat against the pad and plant your feet firmly on the floor.
Grasp the handles with your elbows slightly bent.
Retract your shoulder blades and press them into the backrest.
execution: Exhale and pull the handles together in a smooth arc in front of your chest.
Squeeze your chest muscles hard at the peak contraction.
Inhale and slowly return the handles to the starting position.
Stop when you feel a comfortable stretch in your chest, maintaining control.
cues: Bring your elbows together, not just your hands.
Keep your shoulders pinned back against the pad.
Squeeze your chest as if trying to hold a pen between your pecs.
mistakes: Allowing the shoulders to roll forward at the end of the movement.
Using momentum or letting the weights slam on the stack.
Bending the elbows too much, which reduces the chest stretch.

name: Seated Machine Chest Press
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with the middle of your chest.
Sit back flat against the pad and plant your feet on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down against the pad.
execution: Exhale and press the handles forward until your arms are fully extended but not locked.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back toward your chest.
Keep your elbows tucked slightly below shoulder height.
Stop just before the weight stack touches to maintain constant tension.
cues: Push your back into the pad as you press the handles away.
Keep your chest puffed up throughout the lift.
Control the weight on the way back.
mistakes: Allowing the shoulders to shrug up toward the ears.
Letting the weight stack slam between repetitions.
Using a seat height that is too low, placing stress on the upper shoulders.

name: Hammer Strength Incline Press
target: Clavicular Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest), Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your upper chest.
Sit back firmly against the pad and plant your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with a full overhand grip.
Retract your shoulder blades and keep your chest high.
execution: Exhale and press the handles upward and inward along the machine's guided path.
Extend your arms fully without locking out your elbows.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
Stop when you feel a deep stretch in your upper chest before pressing again.
cues: Drive your upper back into the seat.
Focus on pushing the handles up and together.
Keep your elbows tucked slightly inward.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch excessively off the pad.
Lifting the shoulders off the backrest at the top of the press.
Using too much weight and cutting the range of motion short.

name: Floor Press (Dumbbell)
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
Lie back and bring the dumbbells to the sides of your chest.
Position your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your torso, resting on the floor.
execution: Exhale and press the dumbbells straight up over your chest.
Inhale and lower the dumbbells slowly until your upper arms lightly touch the floor.
Pause for a split second on the floor to eliminate momentum.
Press the weights back up to the starting position.
cues: Press your lower back flat into the floor.
Let your elbows touch the floor gently; do not slam them.
Squeeze your chest at the top of the press.
mistakes: Bouncing the elbows off the floor to gain momentum.
Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees.
Lifting the hips off the floor during the press.

name: Floor Press (Barbell)
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Set up a barbell in a rack at a low height.
Lie flat on your back on the floor under the barbell.
Grip the bar with a medium-wide overhand grip.
Unrack the bar and hold it directly over your chest with locked elbows.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar slowly until your upper arms touch the floor.
Keep your elbows tucked at a 45-degree angle.
Pause briefly on the floor to release elastic energy.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position.
cues: Gently touch your elbows to the floor.
Drive your upper back into the floor.
Keep your wrists straight and strong.
mistakes: Bouncing the elbows off the floor.
Unracking the bar without a spotter if the weight is very heavy.
Allowing the bar to drift too far forward over the stomach.

name: Landmine Press (Single Arm)
target: Clavicular Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest), Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Place one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a corner.
Stand facing the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the end of the barbell in one hand at shoulder height.
Adopt a slightly forward-leaning stance with a tight core.
execution: Exhale and press the barbell upward and forward until your arm is fully extended.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at your shoulder.
Keep your torso stable and avoid twisting as you press.
Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.
cues: Press up and forward in a straight line.
Squeeze your upper chest at the top of the movement.
Keep your core braced to prevent rotation.
mistakes: Using excessive leg drive (turning it into a push press) instead of isolating the chest.
Allowing the torso to twist or lean to the side.
Letting the elbow flare out too wide during the descent.

name: Svend Press
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Clavicular Pectoralis Major
setup: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a light dumbbell (or two small plates) between your palms at chest level.
Squeeze your hands together as hard as possible to create isometric tension in your chest.
Keep your shoulders pulled back and down.
execution: Exhale and slowly press the weight straight out in front of you.
Maintain the inward pressure on the weight throughout the entire movement.
Fully extend your arms while keeping your chest contracted.
Inhale and slowly pull the weight back to your chest, maintaining the squeeze.
cues: Squeeze your hands together as hard as you can.
Keep your chest contracted the entire time.
Move slowly and with control.
mistakes: Losing the inward squeeze, which removes tension from the chest.
Moving too quickly and using momentum.
Using a weight that is too heavy, which strains the shoulders.

name: Standing Cable Press
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Core
setup: Set the pulleys on a cable machine to chest height.
Grasp the handles and step forward into a staggered stance.
Hold the handles at the sides of your chest with your elbows bent.
Brace your core and keep your torso upright.
execution: Exhale and press the handles straight forward, bringing them close together.
Inhale and slowly return the handles to the starting position.
Keep your elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Maintain a stable, non-moving torso throughout the exercise.
cues: Press your hands together at the end of the movement.
Keep your core tight to resist the pull of the cables.
Control the weight on the way back.
mistakes: Leaning too far forward or backward to move the weight.
Allowing the elbows to flare up to shoulder height.
Using a weight that pulls you off balance.

name: Deficit Push-Ups
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Place two elevated platforms (like push-up handles, weight plates, or blocks) on the floor.
Place your hands on the platforms slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step your feet back into a high plank position.
Engage your core and glutes to form a straight line.
execution: Inhale and lower your chest slowly between the platforms.
Go past the level of your hands to achieve a deep stretch in your chest.
Keep your elbows tucked at a 45-degree angle.
Exhale and press through your hands to return to the starting position.
cues: Feel the deep stretch in your chest at the bottom.
Keep your body rigid and straight.
Press up explosively but under control.
mistakes: Sagging at the hips to make the movement easier.
Going too deep too quickly without adequate shoulder mobility.
Flaring the elbows out wide.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
target: Sternal Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Core
setup: Lie flat on a bench holding a single dumbbell in one hand.
Plant both feet firmly on the floor to stabilize your body.
Hold the dumbbell at the side of your chest with your elbow at a 45-degree angle.
Place your free hand on your hip or extend it out to the side for balance.
execution: Exhale and press the dumbbell straight up over your chest.
Inhale and lower the dumbbell slowly to the side of your chest.
Focus on keeping your torso flat on the bench without tilting.
Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.
cues: Brace your core to prevent your body from rolling off the bench.
Drive your feet hard into the floor.
Keep your wrist stacked over your elbow.
mistakes: Allowing the body to tilt or twist toward the weighted side.
Flaring the elbow out to 90 degrees.
Lifting the opposite hip or shoulder off the bench.

name: Pec Deck Flyes (Machine Flyes)
setup: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are level with your mid-chest.
Sit back flat against the pad and grip the handles.
Place your forearms flat against the pads (if using a forearm-pad style machine) or hold the handles with slightly bent elbows.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and retract your shoulder blades.
execution: Squeeze your chest to bring the handles or pads together in front of you.
Hold the contraction at the center for a second, squeezing your chest hard.
Slowly return to the starting position, feeling a stretch in your chest.
Stop the backward movement before your shoulders feel excessive strain.
cues: Bring your elbows together, not just your hands.
Keep your chest puffed out and shoulders back.
Control the weight; do not let the plates slam.
mistakes: Allowing the shoulders to roll forward at the end of the movement.
Using too much weight, which leads to partial reps and shoulder strain.
Letting the weight stack slam between repetitions.

name: Chest Press Machine
target: Sternal Pectorals, Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii
setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your mid-to-lower chest.
Sit back firmly against the backrest and plant your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with a full overhand grip.
Retract your shoulder blades and keep your chest elevated.
execution: Exhale and press the handles forward until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the handles back toward your chest, maintaining control.
Stop just before the weight stack touches to keep constant tension.
cues: Push your back into the seat as you press forward.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Focus on pushing through the palms of your hands.
mistakes: Allowing the upper back to round and shoulders to shrug forward.
Using a rapid, uncontrolled tempo.
Setting the seat too low, which places excessive stress on the anterior deltoids.

name: Push-Ups (Standard)
target: Sternal Pectorals, Anterior Deltoids, Triceps Brachii, Core
setup: Get into a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Place your feet together or slightly apart for stability.
Engage your core, glutes, and quads to form a straight line from head to heels.
Keep your gaze focused slightly in front of your hands to maintain a neutral neck.
execution: Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked at a 45-degree angle.
Descend until your chest is just an inch off the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Push through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
cues: Keep your body as rigid as a board.
Push the floor away from you.
Don't let your hips sag or your lower back arch.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees, which strains the shoulders.
Allowing the hips to sag, which places stress on the lumbar spine.
Performing half-repetitions by not lowering the chest close enough to the floor.

name: Weighted Dips
target: Lower Pectorals, Sternal Pectorals, Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Attach a weight plate to a dip belt and secure it around your waist (or hold a dumbbell between your feet).
Grasp the parallel bars and hoist yourself up to the starting position with locked elbows.
Lean your torso forward at roughly a 30-degree angle.
Pull your shoulders down and back, keeping your neck neutral.
execution: Lower your body slowly by bending your elbows, maintaining the forward torso lean.
Descend until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows, feeling a deep stretch in your chest.
Ensure the weight remains stable and does not swing.
Push through your palms to return to the starting position, squeezing your chest at the top.
cues: Keep the weight stable and prevent it from swinging.
Lean forward to target the chest rather than the triceps.
Control the descent strictly.
mistakes: Dropping down too quickly, which can cause severe shoulder strain under load.
Staying too upright, which shifts the load to the triceps.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.

name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
target: Erector Spinae, Latissimus Dorsi, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, with the barbell positioned over the middle of your feet.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees slightly to grip the bar with a shoulder-width, overhand or mixed grip.
Flatten your back, pull your shoulder blades down and back, and engage your core.
Lower your hips slightly until your shins touch the bar, keeping your chest up and gaze forward.
execution: Drive through your heels, pushing the floor away to initiate the upward movement.
Keep the bar close to your shins and thighs as you stand up to a fully erect position.
Squeeze your glutes and lock out your hips at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
Reverse the movement by hinging at your hips and lowering the bar under control back to the floor.
cues: Push the floor away with your feet.
Keep the bar scraping your shins.
Pack your armpits as if squeezing oranges.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back during the lift.
Allowing the bar to drift away from the body.
Hyperextending the spine at the top lockout.

name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
target: Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Middle Trapezius, Rear Deltoids
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with a shoulder-width, overhand grip.
Hinge forward at your hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat.
Allow the barbell to hang at arm's length in front of you, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back to establish a stable starting position.
execution: Pull the barbell toward your lower chest or upper abdomen, leading the movement with your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together tightly at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a brief second to maximize muscle engagement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
cues: Pull with your elbows, not your hands.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Keep your torso stationary throughout the lift.
mistakes: Using momentum or bouncing the torso up and down.
Rounding the lower or upper back.
Pulling the bar too high toward the collarbone.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
target: Latissimus Dorsi, Teres Major, Rhomboids, Lower Trapezius
setup: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip (palms facing away) wider than shoulder-width.
Hang freely from the bar with your arms fully extended and feet off the floor.
Cross your ankles behind you and bend your knees slightly if necessary.
Depress your shoulder blades and engage your core to stabilize your body.
execution: Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down toward your ribs.

execution: Pull the barbell up toward your lower abdomen/belly button.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides as you pull.
Squeeze your lats and mid-back hard at the top of the movement.
Lower the barbell under control back to the starting position.
cues: Pull the bar to your belt line.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Maintain a proud chest and flat back.
mistakes: Standing completely upright, turning it into a shrug.
Allowing the wrists to curl excessively at the top.
Rounding the lower back.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
Start in a dead hang with your arms fully extended and core engaged.
Keep your legs straight and squeeze your glutes to stabilize your body.
Ensure your shoulders are relaxed and touching your ears.
execution: Pull your shoulder blades down and back to lift your body slightly.
Keep your arms completely straight throughout the entire movement.
Hold the contracted position at the top for a brief second.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting dead hang position.
cues: Pull your shoulders away from your ears.
Do not bend your elbows.
Focus on moving only your shoulder blades.
mistakes: Bending the elbows to pull yourself up.
Using momentum or swinging the legs.
Rushing through the movement without holding the contraction.

name: Single-Arm Cable Row
setup: Attach a single D-handle to a cable pulley set at mid-chest height.
Stand or kneel facing the pulley, gripping the handle with one hand.
Step back to create tension, extending your arm fully with a neutral grip.
Brace your core and stand with a stable, athletic stance.
execution: Pull the handle toward your lower ribs by driving your elbow backward.
Keep your torso square and resist the urge to rotate your body.
Squeeze your lat and shoulder blade at the end of the movement.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position, allowing a slight stretch.
cues: Drive your elbow straight back.
Keep your shoulders square to the machine.
Squeeze your back, not your biceps.
mistakes: Rotating the torso excessively to pull the weight.
Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear.
Letting the weight stack slam on the return.

name: Deficit Deadlift
target: Erector Spinae, Latissimus Dorsi, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings
setup: Stand on a platform or weight plate (1 to 3 inches high) placed on the floor.
Position your feet hip-width apart with the barbell over your mid-foot.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees deeper than a standard deadlift to grip the bar.
Flatten your back, pull your shoulders down, and brace your core tightly.
execution: Drive through your heels to push the floor away, initiating the lift with your legs.
Keep the bar close to your shins as you rise through the increased range of motion.
Extend your hips and knees to stand tall, locking out at the top.
Hinge at your hips and lower the bar under control back to the floor.
cues: Push the floor away.
Keep your chest up and back flat.
Maintain tightness in your lats throughout the lift.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back due to the deeper starting position.
Allowing the hips to rise too fast, turning it into a stiff-legged lift.
Using too high of a deficit, compromising form.

name: Barbell Back Squat
setup: Set the barbell in a squat rack at mid-chest height.
Step under the bar, placing it across your upper traps, and grip the bar firmly with both hands.
Unrack the bar by extending your legs and take two steps backward to establish your stance.
Position your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with toes pointed slightly outward.
execution: Inhale deeply, brace your core, and initiate the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower your body under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through your mid-foot to reverse the movement, extending your hips and knees.
Exhale as you return to the starting standing position, keeping your spine neutral.
cues: Spread the floor with your feet.
Keep your chest proud and eyes forward.
Drive your knees outward as you descend.
mistakes: Allowing the knees to cave inward (valgus collapse).
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the squat (butt wink).
Shifting weight onto the toes, lifting the heels off the ground.

name: Barbell Front Squat
target: Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Core, Upper Back
setup: Set the barbell in a squat rack at shoulder height.
Step forward and position the bar across the front of your shoulders, resting it on your clavicles and deltoids.
Use a clean grip (fingertips under the bar) or a cross-arm grip to secure the bar, keeping elbows high.
Unrack the bar, step back, and set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes slightly flared.
execution: Brace your core, keep your elbows pointing forward, and lower your hips down and back.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, maintaining an upright torso.
Drive through your mid-foot to push yourself back up to the starting position.
Keep your elbows elevated throughout the entire movement to prevent the bar from rolling.
cues: Keep your elbows pointing high.
Stay tall through your chest.
Sit straight down between your knees.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to drop, which causes the upper back to round and the bar to slip.
Initiating the movement by pushing the hips too far back, leading to excessive forward lean.
Allowing the heels to lift off the floor during the descent.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Pull your shoulders back and down, and engage your core.
Unlock your knees slightly, keeping them in a fixed, semi-flexed position.
Keep your gaze forward and slightly down to maintain a neutral neck.
execution: Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back as far as possible, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Lower the bar under control along your thighs and shins until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Maintain a flat back and neutral spine throughout the entire descent.
Drive your hips forward and contract your glutes to return to the starting standing position.
cues: Shave your legs with the barbell.
Push your hips back as if trying to touch a wall behind you.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of the movement.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back, which shifts the load from the hamstrings to the lumbar spine.
Bending the knees too much, turning the exercise into a conventional squat.
Allowing the barbell to drift away from the body, increasing lower back strain.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
setup: Stand about two feet in front of a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Reach one foot back and place the top of your foot flat on the bench behind you.
Align your front foot so that it is directly under your hip or slightly wider for balance.
Engage your core and keep your chest upright.
execution: Lower your hips by bending your front knee, allowing your back knee to sink toward the floor.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the ground, keeping your front knee aligned with your toes.
Drive through the heel of your front foot to push yourself back up to the starting position.
Complete all repetitions on one leg before switching to the other.
cues: Drive through the front heel.
Keep your torso upright or slightly leaned forward for more glute emphasis.
Control the descent; do not let the back knee slam into the floor.
mistakes: Placing the front foot too close to the bench, causing the front knee to push excessively past the toes.
Losing balance due to placing the rear foot directly in line with the front foot (narrow stance).
Using the back leg to push up instead of focusing the effort on the front leg.

name: Leg Press
setup: Sit in the leg press machine and place your feet flat on the sled, shoulder-width apart.
Adjust the seat back so that you can achieve a deep range of motion without your lower back lifting.
Grasp the safety handles at your sides and disengage the safety locks.
Keep your head and upper back pressed firmly against the seat pad.
execution: Inhale and slowly lower the sled by bending your knees until they form a 90-degree angle.
Ensure your knees remain aligned with your toes and do not cave inward.
Exhale and press the sled away by extending your legs, driving through your mid-foot and heels.
Stop just short of locking out your knees at the top of the movement.
cues: Keep your lower back glued to the seat.
Push through your heels.
Do not lock out your knees at the top.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back or pelvis to lift off the seat pad at the bottom of the movement (butt wink).
Locking out the knees aggressively at the top, which transfers the load to the joint.
Using an excessively short range of motion with too much weight.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
setup: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly out.
Hold a dumbbell vertically by one of its ends, cupping it with both hands close to your chest.
Pull your shoulders back and down, and brace your core.
Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing down toward the floor.
execution: Inhale, push your hips back, and bend your knees to lower your body into a squat.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower, keeping your chest upright.
Allow your elbows to track inside your knees at the bottom of the squat.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, exhaling at the top.
cues: Keep the dumbbell glued to your chest.
Pry your knees apart with your elbows at the bottom.
Stay tall and proud through your chest.
mistakes: Allowing the upper back to round and the dumbbell to pull the torso forward.
Allowing the knees to cave inward during the descent or ascent.
Lifting the heels off the floor, shifting the weight onto the toes.

name: Dumbbell Walking Lunges
setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Engage your core, pull your shoulders back, and look straight ahead.
Ensure you have a clear path of at least 10-15 feet in front of you.
Keep your hands relaxed but secure on the dumbbells.
execution: Take a controlled step forward with your right foot, landing heel first.
Lower your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee is just above the ground.
Push off with your left foot, stepping forward to bring your feet together or directly into the next lunge.
Repeat the movement by stepping forward with your left foot.
cues: Step wide enough to maintain balance, like walking on train tracks.
Keep your torso upright and shoulders stacked over your hips.
Drive through the front heel to move forward.
mistakes: Stepping in a straight line (tightrope walking), which causes instability and loss of balance.
Allowing the front knee to collapse inward or push excessively past the toes.
Leaning too far forward, which places excessive stress on the lower back and knees.

name: Lying Leg Curl
setup: Lie face down on the leg curl machine, aligning your knees with the machine's pivot point.
Position the roller pad just below your calf muscles, a few inches above your heels.
Grasp the handles at the front of the machine to secure your upper body.
Keep your torso flat against the bench and engage your core.
execution: Exhale and curl your legs upward by flexing your knees, pulling your heels toward your glutes.
Squeeze your hamstrings hard at the top of the movement for a brief second.
Inhale and slowly lower the roller pad back to the starting position under control.
Maintain tension on the hamstrings by not letting the weight stack touch at the bottom.
cues: Keep your hips pressed firmly into the pad.
Pull with your hamstrings, not your lower back.
Control the weight on the way down.
mistakes: Allowing the hips to lift off the pad, which recruits the lower back and reduces hamstring activation.
Using momentum or swinging the weight instead of controlling the contraction.
Setting the roller pad too high on the calves or too low on the feet.

name: Leg Extension
setup: Sit in the leg extension machine and adjust the backrest so your knees align with the pivot point.
Position the shin pad just above your ankles, on the lower part of your shins.
Grip the handles on the sides of the seat to anchor your hips and upper body.
Ensure your feet are pointing straight ahead and your back is flat against the pad.
execution: Exhale and extend your legs fully by contracting your quadriceps.
Hold the peak contraction at the top of the movement for a brief second.
Inhale and slowly lower the weight back to the starting position under control.
Avoid letting the weight stack slam between repetitions to maintain constant tension.
cues: Squeeze your quads hard at the top.
Keep your hips glued to the seat.
Control the descent; do not let the weight drop.
mistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight up rather than using a controlled muscle contraction.
Allowing the hips to lift off the seat, which reduces the isolation of the quadriceps.
Locking out the knees too aggressively with excessively heavy weight.

name: Standing Calf Raise
setup: Adjust the shoulder pads of the standing calf raise machine to fit your height.
Place the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform, with your heels hanging off.
Stand tall, aligning your shoulders, hips, and ankles in a straight line.
Hold the handles and disengage the safety bar.
execution: Lower your heels slowly as far as possible to feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the stretch to eliminate elastic recoil.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible, contracting your calves.
Hold the peak contraction at the top for a second before slowly lowering down.
cues: Push straight up through your big toes.
Pause at the bottom to stretch, pause at the top to squeeze.
Keep your knees straight but not locked out.
mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom of the movement, which uses tendon elasticity rather than muscle strength.
Bending the knees during the raise, which shifts the focus away from the gastrocnemius.
Using a limited range of motion and not achieving a full stretch or contraction.

name: Seated Calf Raise
setup: Sit on the machine and place the balls of your feet on the platform with your heels hanging off.
Adjust the knee pad so that it rests firmly across your lower thighs, just above your knees.
Place your hands on top of the knee pad handles and lift the weight slightly to release the safety bar.
Keep your torso upright and core engaged.
execution: Lower your heels slowly toward the floor until you feel a full stretch in your calves and Achilles tendon.
Pause for a second at the bottom of the movement.
Explode upward by pushing through the balls of your feet, raising your heels as high as possible.
Squeeze your calves at the top of the movement before beginning the next descent.
cues: Drive through the balls of your feet.
Emphasize the stretch at the bottom.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
mistakes: Bouncing the weight rapidly, which relies on the Achilles tendon's stretch reflex.
Using too much weight, leading to a cut-short range of motion.
Allowing the feet to slip off the platform due to poor positioning.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a flat bench.
Roll a loaded barbell over your legs until it sits directly in your hip crease (use a pad for comfort).
Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, about shoulder-width apart.
Grip the barbell on both sides to keep it stable.
execution: Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.
Raise your hips until your thighs and torso are in a straight line, parallel to the floor.
Ensure your shins are vertical at the top of the movement (90-degree angle at the knees).
Lower your hips back down under control, keeping your chin tucked and eyes looking forward.
cues: Drive through your heels.
Keep your chin tucked and look forward throughout the movement.
Squeeze your glutes like you're pinching a coin at the top.
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top of the movement instead of achieving hip extension.
Placing the feet too far forward (emphasizes hamstrings) or too far back (emphasizes quads).
Allowing the knees to cave inward during the drive phase.

name: Sumo Deadlift
setup: Stand with a very wide stance, feet positioned close to the barbell plates with toes flared outward.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower your torso, gripping the bar inside your knees.
Keep your hands directly beneath your shoulders with a straight-arm grip.
Pull your chest up, flatten your back, and pull the slack out of the bar.
execution: Drive your feet hard into the floor, pushing the ground away to initiate the lift.
Keep the barbell as close to your shins and thighs as possible as it rises.
Extend your hips and knees simultaneously, locking out in an upright standing position.
Lower the bar back to the floor by hinging at the hips and then bending the knees once the bar clears them.
cues: Spread the floor with your feet.
Pull your chest up and drop your hips.
Keep the bar glued to your body.
mistakes: Allowing the knees to cave inward, which reduces power and increases injury risk.
Rounding the spine, particularly the lower back, during the pull.
Letting the hips rise too quickly, turning the lift into a stiff-legged deadlift.

name: Glute Ham Raise
setup: Adjust the GHR machine so your knees rest slightly behind the curved pad when your feet are locked in.
Place your feet flat against the footplate between the rollers.
Start in an upright position with your knees bent at 90 degrees and your torso vertical.
Cross your arms over your chest and engage your core.
execution: Slowly lower your torso forward by extending your knees, keeping your hips locked in extension.
Descend until your body is in a straight line, parallel to the floor.
Pull yourself back up by flexing your knees and contracting your hamstrings.
Return to the starting vertical position, maintaining a straight line from head to knees.
cues: Push your toes into the footplate.
Keep your hips fully extended throughout.
Pull yourself up using only your hamstrings.
mistakes: Bending or hinging at the hips to make the movement easier, which reduces hamstring load.
Using momentum or swinging the upper body to complete the repetition.
Hyperextending the lower back at the top of the movement.

name: Dumbbell Step-Ups
setup: Stand tall in front of a sturdy box or bench that is knee-height.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back.
Place your entire right foot flat on top of the box.
execution: Drive through your right heel to lift your body up onto the box.
Bring your left foot to meet your right foot on top of the box, standing fully upright.
Step back down with your left foot under control, followed by your right foot.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch leading legs.
cues: Keep your weight on the heel of the working foot.
Do not push off with your trailing foot.
Stand up tall at the top of the box.
mistakes: Using the trailing leg to jump or push off the floor instead of using the lead leg.
Allowing the knee of the working leg to collapse inward during the step-up.
Leaning too far forward, which shifts the focus away from the legs and onto the lower back.

name: Machine Hack Squat
setup: Position yourself in the hack squat machine, placing your back flat against the backrest.
Place your shoulders firmly under the padded shoulder supports.
Position your feet on the platform, shoulder-width apart and slightly forward.
Disengage the safety handles and hold them for stability.
execution: Inhale and slowly lower your body by bending your knees, keeping your back flat against the pad.
Descend until your thighs form a 90-degree angle or slightly lower.
Exhale and drive through your heels to push the carriage back up to the starting position.
Stop just short of locking out your knees at the top.
cues: Keep your back and hips glued to the pad.
Drive through your heels.
Push your knees outward as you descend.
mistakes: Allowing the heels to lift off the platform, which places excessive stress on the knees.
Allowing the lower back or glutes to lift off the backrest at the bottom of the movement.
Locking out the knees aggressively at the top of the exercise.

name: Kettlebell Swing
setup: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with a kettlebell on the floor about a foot in front of you.
Hinge at your hips, bend your knees slightly, and grip the kettlebell handle with both hands.
Pull your shoulders back and down, and engage your lats.
Tilt the kettlebell toward you, preparing to hike it back.
execution: Swing (hike) the kettlebell back between your legs, close to your groin.
Snap your hips forward powerfully, contracting your glutes and hamstrings to stand up tall.
Allow the momentum to swing the kettlebell up to chest height, keeping your arms loose.
Let the kettlebell fall back down naturally, hinging at the hips to catch it and repeat.
cues: Hinge at the hips, don't squat.
Snap your hips forward like a spring.
Keep your core tight at the top of the swing.
mistakes: Squatting the weight up and down instead of hinging at the hips.
Using the shoulders and arms to pull the kettlebell up instead of using hip power.
Hyperextending the lower back at the top of the swing.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
setup: Kneel on a padded surface or yoga mat.
Secure your ankles under a heavy object, a partner's hands, or a specialized Nordic strap.
Align your torso so that it is completely upright, forming a straight line from your knees to your head.
Hold your hands in front of your chest, ready to catch yourself.
execution: Slowly lower your torso toward the floor by extending your knees, resisting gravity with your hamstrings.
Maintain a straight line through your hips and torso; do not bend at the waist.
Lower yourself as slowly as possible until you can no longer support your weight.
Catch yourself with your hands on the floor, push off slightly, and use your hamstrings to pull yourself back up.
cues: Resist the fall as long as possible.
Keep your hips locked straight.
Use your hands only to assist the return.
mistakes: Bending at the hips (breaking the line) to make the descent easier.
Falling too fast without actively resisting with the hamstrings.
Failing to catch oneself safely, risking injury to the face or chest.

name: Barbell Box Squat
setup: Place a box or bench behind you in the squat rack, adjusted to your desired squat depth.
Unrack the barbell across your upper traps and step back until your calves are close to the box.
Set your feet in a wide stance, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
execution: Initiate the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower yourself under control until your glutes make contact with the box.
Pause briefly on the box, releasing hip flexor tension while keeping your core tightly braced.
Drive through your heels and explode upward to return to the starting position.
cues: Sit back, not down.
Pause on the box without relaxing your core.
Drive your knees out as you stand up.
mistakes: Rocking back on the box to gain momentum for the ascent.
Plop-sitting onto the box too quickly without controlling the descent.
Allowing the spine to round or collapse while sitting on the box.

name: Pistol Squat
setup: Stand tall on one leg, with the other leg extended straight out in front of you.
Extend your arms forward at shoulder height to help maintain balance.
Engage your core and fix your gaze on a point in front of you.
Keep the foot of your supporting leg flat on the floor.
execution: Inhale and slowly lower your hips back and down, bending the knee of your supporting leg.
Keep the non-supporting leg elevated and straight throughout the descent.
Descend until your thigh is below parallel, keeping your heel firmly planted.
Exhale and drive through the heel of your supporting leg to return to the standing position.
cues: Keep your heel glued to the floor.
Reach your arms and non-working leg forward for balance.
Control the descent all the way down.
mistakes: Allowing the heel of the supporting foot to lift off the ground.
Allowing the knee of the supporting leg to collapse inward (valgus).
Rounding the spine excessively or collapsing the chest forward.

name: Seated Leg Curl
setup: Sit in the machine and adjust the backrest so your knees align with the pivot point.
Place the back of your lower legs on top of the padded lever, just below your calves.
Lower the thigh support pad so it rests firmly against your thighs to secure you.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the machine and sit tall.
execution: Exhale and pull the lever down and back toward your glutes by flexing your knees.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the point of maximum contraction.
Inhale and slowly return the lever to the starting position under control.
Maintain tension on the hamstrings by not letting the weight stack touch.
cues: Pull your heels back as far as possible.
Keep your thighs pressed firmly against the pad.
Control the return of the weight.
mistakes: Allowing the thighs to lift off the seat due to loose pad adjustment.
Using jerky movements or momentum to move the weight.
Failing to go through a full range of motion.

name: Cable Pull-Through
setup: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley machine.
Stand facing away from the machine, with the cable running between your legs.
Take a few steps forward to create tension on the cable, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the rope handles with both hands, arms extended down.
execution: Hinge at your hips and push them back toward the machine, keeping a slight bend in your knees.
Allow your arms to travel back between your legs, maintaining a flat back.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to an upright standing position.
Keep your arms straight and relaxed; do not pull the weight with your upper body.
cues: Reach back through your legs.
Snap your hips forward to stand up.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
mistakes: Squatting the weight instead of hinging at the hips.
Using the arms and shoulders to pull the rope forward.
Rounding the lower back during the hinge phase.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
setup: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in your right hand (or both hands) with feet hip-width apart.
Shift your weight onto your left leg, keeping a slight bend in the knee.
Engage your core and find your balance.
Keep your shoulders back and down.
execution: Hinge forward at your hips, extending your right leg straight behind you for balance.
Lower the dumbbell toward the floor, keeping it close to your supporting leg.
Descend until your torso and back leg are parallel to the floor, keeping your hips square.
Drive through your left heel and squeeze your glutes to return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your hips square to the floor.
Reach your back heel toward the wall behind you.
Keep the dumbbell close to your leg.
mistakes: Allowing the hips to rotate or open up to the side during the hinge.
Rounding the spine, particularly the lower back, to reach for the floor.
Losing balance due to rushing the movement.

name: Cossack Squat
setup: Stand with an extremely wide stance, feet about double shoulder-width apart.
Point your toes slightly outward.
Keep your torso upright and hands held in front of your chest for balance.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back.
execution: Shift your weight to your right side, bending your right knee and pushing your hips back.
Keep your left leg completely straight, allowing the left toes to pivot upward toward the ceiling.
Lower your hips as deep as your mobility allows, keeping your right heel flat on the floor.
Drive through your right foot to return to the starting wide stance, then repeat on the other side.
cues: Keep the heel of the working foot flat on the floor.
Sit back and down into the hip.
Keep your chest as upright as possible.
mistakes: Allowing the heel of the squatting leg to lift off the floor.
Rounding the spine and collapsing the chest forward.
Failing to keep the non-working leg straight.

name: Zercher Squat
target: Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Core, Upper Back
setup: Set the barbell in a squat rack at about elbow height.
Hook the bar into the crooks of your elbows, holding your forearms up and hands together.
Unrack the bar, step back, and set your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Brace your core and keep your upper back tight.
execution: Inhale, push your hips back, and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
Descend until your elbows touch your thighs or pass inside your knees.
Maintain an upright torso and do not let the bar pull you forward.
Drive through your mid-foot to return to the starting position, exhaling at the top.
cues: Pull the bar tight against your body.
Keep your chest up and elbows high.
Drive your knees out as you stand.
mistakes: Allowing the bar to drift away from the body, placing extreme stress on the lower back.
Rounding the upper back and shoulders under the weight.
Allowing the knees to cave inward during the ascent.

name: Smith Machine Squat
setup: Set the Smith machine bar to shoulder height.
Step under the bar, placing it across your upper traps, and grip it with both hands.
Position your feet slightly forward of the bar, shoulder-width apart.
Rotate the bar to unlock it from the safety pegs.
execution: Inhale and lower your hips down and back, bending your knees.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat against the imaginary vertical plane.
Drive through your heels to push yourself back up to the starting position.
Exhale at the top of the movement, keeping your core braced.
cues: Lean back slightly into the bar.
Drive through your heels.
Keep your chest up.
mistakes: Placing the feet too far back, causing the knees to push excessively past the toes.
Allowing the knees to cave inward during the lift.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the squat.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
setup: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Pull your shoulders back and down, and engage your core.
Unlock your knees slightly, keeping them in a fixed, semi-flexed position.
Keep your gaze forward and slightly down.
execution: Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back as far as possible, keeping the dumbbells close to your legs.
Lower the dumbbells under control along your thighs and shins until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Maintain a flat back and neutral spine throughout the entire descent.
Drive your hips forward and contract your glutes to return to the starting standing position.
cues: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs.
Push your hips back as if trying to touch a wall behind you.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back, which shifts the load from the hamstrings to the lumbar spine.
Bending the knees too much, turning the exercise into a squat.
Allowing the dumbbells to drift away from the body.

name: Sled Push
setup: Load the sled with the desired weight.
Grip the high handles of the sled with your arms fully extended or bent, depending on preference.
Lean forward at a 45-degree angle, creating a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and place your feet in a staggered stance.
execution: Drive through your front foot to push the sled forward.
Take powerful, alternating steps, driving your knees forward with each stride.
Maintain a consistent forward lean and keep your spine neutral.
Continue pushing for the desired distance or time.
cues: Drive the ground away behind you.
Keep your core tight and spine straight.
Keep your hips low.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to round or sag during the push.
Taking steps that are too short or too long, reducing power output.
Losing the forward lean and standing too upright.

name: Bodyweight Wall Sit
setup: Stand with your back against a flat wall, feet about two feet away from the wall.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart.
Slide your back down the wall until your hips and knees are at a 90-degree angle.
Ensure your knees are directly above your ankles, not your toes.
execution: Hold this position, keeping your back and head flat against the wall.
Keep your core engaged and hands resting on your thighs or crossed over your chest.
Breathe deeply and hold the position for the target duration.
To finish, slide back up the wall to a standing position.
cues: Press your lower back firmly into the wall.
Keep your knees at a 90-degree angle.
Do not let your knees cave inward.
mistakes: Allowing the knees to push past the toes, placing excessive stress on the joints.
Resting the hands on the knees to support the weight, reducing quad activation.
Not sliding down far enough, making the exercise too easy.

name: Barbell Overhead Squat
setup: Hold a barbell overhead with a very wide (snatch) grip.
Press the bar up actively, locking your elbows and shrugging your shoulders to secure the weight.
Set your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly out.
Brace your core and find your balance.
execution: Inhale, push your hips back, and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
Keep the barbell positioned directly over your mid-foot throughout the descent.
Descend until your thighs are below parallel, maintaining an upright torso.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, keeping the bar locked overhead.
cues: Push up actively into the bar.
Keep the bar directly over your mid-foot.
Stay tall and proud through your chest.
mistakes: Allowing the barbell to drift forward, causing loss of balance and shoulder strain.
Allowing the elbows to bend or shoulders to relax during the squat.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the movement.

name: Leg Extensions
target: Quadriceps (Rectus Femoris, Vastus Lateralis, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Intermedius)
setup: Adjust the back pad of the leg extension machine so your knees align perfectly with the pivot point of the machine.
Position the lower shin pad so it rests just above your ankles.
Sit back firmly against the pad and grip the handles on the sides of the seat.
Select an appropriate weight and place your feet pointing straight forward.
execution: Initiate the movement by contracting your quadriceps to extend your legs upward.
Raise the weight under control until your legs are fully extended and parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your quadriceps hard at the top of the movement for a brief second.
Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position, maintaining tension on the quads.
Avoid letting the weight stack touch between repetitions.
cues: Squeeze your quads hard at the top.
Pull yourself down into the seat using the handles.
Control the weight on the way down.
mistakes: Using momentum or swinging the weight up instead of using controlled muscle contraction.
Allowing the hips to lift off the seat during the extension.
Setting the shin pad too high on the shins or too low on the feet.

name: Goblet Squat
setup: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly out.
Hold a dumbbell vertically by one of its ends, cupping it with both hands close to your chest.
Pull your shoulders back and down, and brace your core.
Keep your elbows pointing down toward the floor.
execution: Begin the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower, keeping your chest upright.
Ensure your elbows track inside your knees at the bottom of the squat.
Drive through your heels and mid-foot to return to the standing position.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and repeat.
cues: Keep the dumbbell glued to your chest.
Push your knees out to make room for your torso.
Stay tall and don't let your chest cave.
mistakes: Allowing the upper back to round and the dumbbell to pull the torso forward.
Letting the knees cave inward during the descent or ascent.
Lifting the heels off the ground, shifting the weight to the toes.

name: Barbell Sumo Deadlift
target: Gluteus Maximus, Adductors, Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Erector Spinae
setup: Stand with a very wide stance, feet positioned close to the weight plates with toes flared outward.
Bend at your hips and knees to lower your torso and grip the barbell with a shoulder-width, overhand or mixed grip.
Position your shins vertically, close to or touching the bar.
Pull your chest up, flatten your back, and pull the slack out of the bar.
execution: Initiate the lift by driving your feet hard into the floor, spreading the floor apart.
Keep the bar as close to your shins and thighs as possible as you ascend.
Drive your hips forward to lock out the lift, standing completely upright.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
Lower the bar under control by reversing the movement, keeping it close to your body.
cues: Spread the floor with your feet.
Pull your chest up and drop your hips close to the bar.
Keep the bar close to your body.
mistakes: Allowing the knees to cave inward during the initial pull.
Rounding the lower back, which increases the risk of injury.
Hips rising too fast, turning the lift into a stiff-legged deadlift.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
setup: Sit in the leg press machine and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform.
Ensure your heels hang off the bottom of the platform completely.
Push the platform up and disengage the safety locks, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Grasp the handles on the sides of the seat for stability.
execution: Lower the platform slowly by flexing your ankles, feeling a deep stretch in your calves.
Pause at the bottom of the stretch for one to two seconds to eliminate momentum.
Push the platform away by extending your ankles, raising your heels as high as possible.
Squeeze your calves hard at the peak contraction before slowly lowering again.
cues: Push through the balls of your feet.
Pause at the bottom to stretch.
Keep your knees straight but not locked.
mistakes: Bending and straightening the knees to move the weight instead of using the ankles.
Bouncing the weight at the bottom of the movement.
Allowing the feet to slip off the edge of the platform.

name: Barbell Deficit Deadlift
target: Hamstrings, Gluteus Maximus, Erector Spinae, Quadriceps
setup: Place a stable platform or weight plate (1 to 3 inches high) on the floor.
Stand on top of the platform with your feet hip-width apart.
Position a loaded barbell over the mid-foot of your shoes.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to grip the bar with a shoulder-width grip, flattening your back.
execution: Pull your chest up, engage your lats, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Drive through your feet to push the floor away, initiating the lift with your legs.
Keep the bar close to your shins as you pull it up past your knees.
Extend your hips and knees fully to stand upright, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower the bar under control back to the platform, maintaining a flat back.
cues: Push the floor away.
Keep your back flat and chest up.
Keep the bar close to your body.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back due to the increased range of motion requirement.
Hips rising too quickly, turning the lift into a stiff-legged pull.
Using a deficit that is too high, compromising spinal mechanics.

name: Cable Hip Abduction
target: Gluteus Medius, Gluteus Minimus, Tensor Fasciae Latae
setup: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable pulley.
Stand sideways to the machine, securing the strap to the ankle furthest from the pulley.
Hold onto the machine's frame with one hand for balance.
Keep your standing leg slightly bent and your core engaged.
execution: Sweep your outer leg out to the side away from the machine in a controlled arc.
Keep your hips square and avoid tilting your torso to the side.
Pause for a brief second at the peak of the movement.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position, crossing slightly in front of your standing leg.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
cues: Lead with your heel.
Keep your torso upright and still.
Control the weight on the way back.
mistakes: Leaning the torso excessively to the opposite side to cheat the range of motion.
Swinging the leg with momentum instead of using muscle contraction.
Rotating the foot outward, which shifts the focus to the hip flexors.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Cossack Squat
setup: Stand with an extremely wide stance, feet about double shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell vertically at your chest in a goblet position.
Point your toes slightly outward and brace your core.
Keep your shoulders back and down.
execution: Shift your weight to your right side, bending your right knee and pushing your hips back.
Keep your left leg completely straight, allowing the left foot to pivot on the heel so the toes point up.
Descend as deep as your mobility allows, keeping your right heel flat on the floor.
Drive through your right foot to return to the wide standing starting position.
Repeat on the other side or alternate legs.
cues: Keep the working heel flat on the floor.
Sit back into your hip.
Keep your chest up.
mistakes: Allowing the heel of the bending leg to lift off the floor.
Rounding the spine and collapsing the chest forward.
Failing to keep the non-working leg straight.

name: Sissy Squat
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding onto a sturdy upright object for balance if needed.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Rise up onto the balls of your feet.
Keep your hips locked in extension throughout the movement.
execution: Incline your torso backward while bending your knees, pushing your knees forward and down.
Maintain a straight line from your knees to your head; do not bend at the hips.
Lower yourself until your knees are close to the floor or as deep as comfortable.
Drive through the balls of your feet, contracting your quads to return to the starting position.
Squeeze your quads at the top and repeat.
cues: Push your knees forward and lean your torso back.
Keep your hips locked straight; don't bend at the waist.
Drive through the balls of your feet.
mistakes: Bending at the hips (piking), which removes tension from the quadriceps.
Dropping too fast without control, risking knee strain.
Failing to maintain heel elevation throughout the movement.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Triceps, Upper Trapezius
setup: Set the barbell in a rack at upper-chest height.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with a pronated grip.
Step under the bar, resting it on your anterior deltoids and clavicle.
Unrack the bar and take one to two steps back, establishing a shoulder-width stance.
execution: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and press the bar vertically.
Pull your head back slightly as the bar passes your face to maintain a straight path.
Once the bar clears your head, push your head forward to lock out the weight overhead.
Lower the bar under control back to the starting position on your upper chest.
cues: Squeeze your glutes to protect your lower back.
Drive your head through the window at the top.
Keep your elbows tucked slightly forward, not flared.
mistakes: Excessive arching of the lower back.
Flaring the elbows completely out to the sides.
Using leg drive in a strict press.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
setup: Sit on a bench with a vertical back support.
Place a dumbbell on each knee while sitting upright.
Kick the dumbbells up to shoulder height one at a time.
Rotate your wrists so your palms are facing forward and elbows are bent at 90 degrees.
execution: Brace your core and press the dumbbells vertically overhead.
Bring the dumbbells close together at the top without letting them touch.
Pause briefly at the peak of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position at ear level.
cues: Press straight up, not outward.
Keep your forearms vertical throughout the lift.
Keep your back flat against the pad.
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the bench.
Clanging the dumbbells together at the top.
Lowering the weights too fast without control.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
setup: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing inward.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and lean forward very slightly from the hips.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back and down.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides in a wide arc.
Continue raising the dumbbells until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause for a split second at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position under control.
cues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Pour out a pitcher of water at the top.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
mistakes: Using momentum or swinging the torso to lift the weight.
Raising the hands higher than the elbows.
Shrugging the shoulders up to use the trapezius.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
setup: Set a low pulley on a cable machine to the lowest setting.
Stand sideways to the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Reach across your body to grip the handle with your outer hand.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees and a slight forward lean.
execution: Raise your arm out to the side in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
Lift the cable until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your lateral deltoid at the peak of the contraction.
Slowly lower the handle back across your body to the starting position.
cues: Push the cable away from your body, not just up.
Keep your torso completely still.
Control the negative portion of the lift.
mistakes: Using momentum by jerking the torso.
Letting the shoulder shrug up toward the ear.
Allowing the elbow to bend excessively during the lift.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and a neutral spine.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Hold the peak contraction for a brief second.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
cues: Lead the movement with your elbows.
Focus on pulling the weights out to the walls, not up.
Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor.
mistakes: Swinging the torso to generate momentum.
Using too much weight, leading to a row instead of a fly.
Rounding the lower back during the hinge.

name: Face Pulls
target: Posterior Deltoids, Rotator Cuff, Upper Trapezius
setup: Set a cable pulley at upper-chest or eye height.
Attach a double-rope handle to the pulley.
Grip the rope with an overhand grip (thumbs facing backward).
Take a few steps back to tension the cable and assume a staggered stance.
execution: Pull the center of the rope directly toward your nose or forehead.
As you pull, flare your elbows out and pull your hands apart.
Externally rotate your shoulders at the end of the movement, showing your biceps.
Slowly return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
cues: Pull the rope apart like you are tearing it.
Show your biceps to the mirror at the end.
Keep your chest proud and shoulders down.
mistakes: Using too much weight and leaning back excessively.
Pulling with the hands instead of leading with the elbows.
Rushing the eccentric phase of the movement.

name: Arnold Press
setup: Sit on a bench with a vertical back support.
