Hold a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, palms facing your body.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso, similar to the top of a bicep curl.
Ensure your feet are planted firmly on the floor.
execution: Press the dumbbells overhead while simultaneously rotating your wrists.
As the weights clear your head, your palms should face forward.
Lock out your arms at the top of the movement without touching the weights.
Lower the dumbbells while rotating your wrists back to the starting position.
cues: Rotate smoothly as you press.
Keep your core tight and back flat against the pad.
Control the rotation on the way down.
mistakes: Rotating too early or too late in the movement.
Arching the lower back excessively.
Using a weight that is too heavy, compromising form.

name: Barbell Push Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Triceps, Quadriceps
setup: Set the barbell in a rack at upper-chest height.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with a pronated grip.
Step under the bar, resting it on your anterior deltoids and clavicle.
Unrack the bar, take a step back, and set your feet shoulder-width apart.
execution: Perform a quick, shallow dip by bending your knees slightly (about 3-4 inches).
Explosively drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees.
Transfer that upward momentum into pressing the barbell overhead.
Lock out your arms overhead, then lower the bar under control back to your chest.
cues: Dip straight down like a piston, don't lean forward.
Drive through your heels with maximum power.
Push your head through the window at lockout.
mistakes: Dipping too deep, turning it into a squat.
Leaning forward during the dip phase.
Failing to control the descent of the barbell.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles are aligned with your shoulders.
Sit back firmly against the pad with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the handles with a pronated or neutral grip.
Keep your elbows bent and aligned under your wrists.
execution: Brace your core and press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended.
Avoid locking out your elbows aggressively at the top.
Pause briefly at the peak of the movement.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining tension.
cues: Keep your back flat against the pad.
Drive your hands straight up.
Control the weight on the way down.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch off the seat.
Using a range of motion that is too short.
Letting the weights slam at the bottom of the rep.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
setup: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting against the front of your thighs.
Keep your palms facing your body (pronated grip).
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core.
execution: Raise the dumbbells forward and upward in a controlled arc.
Continue lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
cues: Lift with your shoulders, not your lower back.
Keep your torso completely still.
Control the descent of the weights.
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the dumbbells.
Using excessively heavy weights.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug up toward the ears.

name: Barbell Upright Row
setup: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
Let the bar hang in front of your thighs with arms fully extended.
Keep your chest proud and shoulders pulled back.
execution: Pull the barbell straight up toward your collarbone, keeping it close to your body.
Lead the movement with your elbows, raising them higher than your forearms.
Pause briefly at the top when the bar reaches chest height.
Lower the barbell slowly and under control back to the starting position.
cues: Keep the bar close to your shirt.
Lead with your elbows.
Keep your shoulders down, don't shrug.
mistakes: Pulling the bar too high (above collarbone), risking shoulder impingement.
Using a grip that is too narrow.
Using momentum to swing the weight up.

name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
setup: Set the pulleys of a dual-cable machine at head height.
Remove any handles and grip the bare cable ends.
Stand in the center, reach across your body, and grab the left cable with your right hand and vice versa.
Step back slightly to create tension and stand tall with core engaged.
execution: Pull your arms out and back in a wide horizontal arc.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back at the end of the movement.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position, crossing them over.
cues: Pull your hands out to the side walls.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed.
Control the return of the cables.
mistakes: Bending and extending the elbows (turning it into a tricep extension).
Shrugging the shoulders to use the traps.
Leaning back excessively to pull the weight.

name: Pike Push-Up
setup: Start in a standard push-up position on the floor.
Walk your feet forward while keeping your legs straight, raising your hips into the air.
Your body should form an inverted 'V' shape (pike position).
Keep your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and look at your feet.
execution: Lower your head diagonally forward toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Your head should touch the floor slightly ahead of your hands, forming a tripod.
Press through your palms to push your body back up to the starting position.
Fully extend your arms at the top, pushing your head back between your shoulders.
cues: Lower your head forward, not straight down.
Push the floor away from you.
Keep your hips high throughout the movement.
mistakes: Lowering the head straight down between the hands.
Flaring the elbows out to the sides.
Letting the hips sag during the movement.

name: Handstand Push-Up
setup: Kick up into a handstand against a wall, facing away from the wall.
Place your hands about 6-12 inches away from the wall, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Keep your body straight, core tight, and toes pointed.
Look slightly forward at the floor between your hands.
execution: Lower your body under control by bending your elbows.
Touch the top of your head lightly to the floor.
Keep your elbows tucked at roughly a 45-degree angle.
Press explosively through your palms to return to the starting handstand position.
cues: Keep your core braced and body rigid.
Tuck your elbows, don't flare them.
Push the floor away to lock out.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees.
Arching the lower back excessively against the wall.
Dropping too quickly and crashing your head into the floor.

name: Landmine Press
setup: Place one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment.
Stand facing the barbell with feet shoulder-width apart.
Clean the loaded end of the barbell up to one shoulder, holding it with one hand.
Assume a slight forward lean, keeping your core tight and spine neutral.
execution: Press the barbell upward and forward in a diagonal path.
Fully extend your arm at the top of the movement.
Squeeze your shoulder and upper chest at the peak.
Lower the barbell under control back to the starting position at your shoulder.
cues: Press up and forward, following the natural arc of the bar.
Keep your core braced to prevent twisting.
Lean into the press slightly at the top.
mistakes: Standing too upright, turning it into a strict vertical press.
Allowing the torso to twist during the press.
Using leg drive in a strict press variation.

name: Kettlebell Halos
target: Rotator Cuff, Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Core
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell upside down by the horns.
Hold the kettlebell at chest height, keeping your elbows tucked.
Engage your core, squeeze your glutes, and stand tall.
execution: Begin circling the kettlebell around your head to one side.
Keep the kettlebell close to your neck as it passes behind your head.
Complete the circle, returning the kettlebell to the starting position at your chest.
Alternate directions for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Keep the kettlebell close to your head like a halo.
Do not move your head; move the kettlebell around it.
Keep your core locked down to prevent torso movement.
mistakes: Moving the head back and forth to avoid the kettlebell.
Using a weight that is too heavy, risking shoulder strain.
Allowing the lower back to arch during the movement.

name: Dumbbell Lu Raises
setup: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a pair of light dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing forward.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core.
execution: Raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide, circular arc.
Continue raising the weights all the way overhead until they almost touch.
Rotate your shoulders externally as the weights pass shoulder height.
Slowly reverse the movement, lowering the dumbbells back to the starting position.
cues: Draw a massive circle with the dumbbells.
Keep your shoulders down, even at the top.
Control the descent completely.
mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy.
Rushing through the movement without control.
Failing to rotate the shoulders, causing impingement.

name: Behind the Neck Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Upper Trapezius
setup: Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height.
Step under the bar, resting it across your upper trapezius.
Grip the bar with a wide grip, wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and take a step back, establishing a stable stance.
execution: Brace your core and press the barbell vertically overhead.
Lock out your arms at the top of the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and under control back to your upper traps.
Ensure your head remains neutral throughout the movement.
cues: Press straight up, keeping the bar path vertical.
Keep your core tight to protect your spine.
Control the descent to avoid impact on your neck.
mistakes: Using too much weight, which can cause shoulder injury.
Letting the bar crash onto the neck or traps.
Lacking the shoulder mobility required for this exercise.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
setup: Set a low pulley on a cable machine to the lowest setting.
Stand sideways to the machine, holding the handle with your outer hand.
Place your inner hand on the machine frame for stability.
Keep your feet shoulder-width apart and core engaged.
execution: Raise your outer arm out to the side in a wide arc.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow and lead with your elbow.
Lift until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position under control.
cues: Push the handle away from your body.
Keep your torso completely still.
Focus on the tension in the side of your shoulder.
mistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight.
Shrugging the shoulder up to assist the lift.
Allowing the elbow to bend too much.

name: Dumbbell Y-Raise
target: Lower Trapezius, Posterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids
setup: Set an incline bench to a 30 to 45-degree angle.
Lie chest-down on the bench with your head clearing the top of the pad.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down.
Turn your hands so your palms are facing each other.
execution: Raise your arms up and out at a 45-degree angle, forming a 'Y' shape.
Keep your arms straight and lead with your thumbs pointing upward.
Squeeze your shoulder blades and rear delts at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
cues: Form a 'Y' with your arms.
Lead with your thumbs toward the ceiling.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
mistakes: Raising the arms straight forward instead of in a 'Y'.
Using too much weight, which limits the range of motion.
Shrugging the shoulders excessively.

name: Barbell Front Raise
setup: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a barbell with an overhand grip at thigh level.
Keep your hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back and down.
execution: Raise the barbell forward and upward while keeping your arms straight.
Continue lifting until the bar is at shoulder height or slightly above.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and under control back to your thighs.
cues: Keep your torso completely still.
Lift with your front shoulders, not your back.
Control the descent of the bar.
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the barbell.
Using a grip that is too wide or too narrow.
Allowing the lower back to arch excessively.

name: Seated Barbell Press
setup: Sit on a bench with a vertical back support.
Set the barbell in a rack at upper-chest height in front of you.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with a pronated grip.
Unrack the bar and hold it at collarbone level, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
execution: Brace your core and press the barbell vertically overhead.
Pull your head back slightly as the bar passes your face.
Push your head forward once the bar clears your head to lock out overhead.
Lower the bar slowly back to your upper chest under control.
cues: Keep your forearms vertical under the bar.
Press straight up, not forward.
Keep your back flat against the pad.
mistakes: Arching the lower back off the bench.
Flaring the elbows out to the sides.
Bouncing the bar off the chest.

name: Incline Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
setup: Set an incline bench to a 30 to 45-degree angle.
Lie chest-down on the bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down.
Rotate your wrists so your palms are facing backward.
execution: Row the dumbbells upward by flaring your elbows out to the sides.
Pull until your upper arms are parallel to the floor and elbows are bent at 90 degrees.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
cues: Flare your elbows out wide.
Pull with your elbows, not your hands.
Keep your chest glued to the pad.
mistakes: Tucking the elbows close to the body.
Using too much weight, reducing the range of motion.
Lifting the chest off the bench.

name: Cable Front Raise
setup: Set a low pulley on a cable machine to the lowest setting.
Attach a straight bar or rope handle to the pulley.
Stand facing away from the machine with the cable running between your legs.
Grip the handle with an overhand grip and step forward to create tension.
execution: Raise your arms forward and upward, keeping them straight.
Lift the handle until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position under control.
cues: Keep your core tight and torso upright.
Lift with your front shoulders.
Control the cable on the way down.
mistakes: Leaning backward to help lift the weight.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug up.
Bending the elbows excessively during the lift.

name: Dumbbell Scaption
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Serratus Anterior
setup: Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing slightly forward.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back and down.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Raise your arms upward and forward at a 30-degree angle.
Continue lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
cues: Lift in a 'V' shape, not straight forward or straight out.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed.
Control the movement both up and down.
mistakes: Lifting straight out to the sides or straight forward.
Using too much weight, causing shrugging.
Using momentum to swing the weights.

name: Overhead Barbell Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Triceps, Upper Pectorals
setup: Set the barbell in a rack at upper-chest height.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with an overhand grip.
Step under the bar, resting it on your front shoulders (clavicles), and unrack it.
Take one or two steps back, placing your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
execution: Press the barbell vertically by extending your arms, tilting your head back slightly to clear your chin.
Once the bar clears your head, return your head to its neutral position.
Lock out your elbows at the top of the movement, pushing your head slightly forward ('pushing through the window').
Lower the barbell under control back to the starting position on your upper chest.
Inhale on the way down, and exhale as you press the weight up.
cues: Squeeze your glutes to protect your lower back.
Keep your elbows tucked slightly forward, not flared out to the sides.
Push the floor away with your feet.
Punch the ceiling at the top of the lift.
mistakes: Excessively arching the lower back to assist the lift.
Bouncing the bar off the chest at the bottom of the movement.
Failing to lock out the elbows or complete the full range of motion.

name: Rear Delt Dumbbell Fly
target: Posterior Deltoids, Infraspinatus, Rhomboids, Middle Trapezius
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and maintain a flat, neutral spine.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and lead the movement with your elbows.
Raise the weights until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
Exhale as you raise the weights, and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Lead with your elbows toward the ceiling.
Keep your neck neutral; look at a spot on the floor a few feet in front of you.
Focus on squeezing the back of your shoulders, not just your back muscles.
mistakes: Swinging the torso up and down to create momentum.
Allowing the lower back to round, increasing the risk of injury.
Tucking the chin to the chest or hyperextending the neck.

name: Cable Face Pulls
target: Posterior Deltoids, Rotator Cuff, Upper Trapezius, Rhomboids
setup: Set a cable pulley to upper-chest or forehead height.
Attach a double-D rope handle to the pulley.
Grip the rope with your thumbs facing backward (neutral or overhand grip).
Step back from the machine to lift the weight stack, and stand with a stable, staggered stance.
Extend your arms fully in front of you, keeping your shoulders pulled back.
execution: Pull the center of the rope directly toward your nose or forehead.
As you pull, flare your elbows out and pull the ends of the rope apart.
At the end of the movement, externally rotate your shoulders so your hands are higher than your elbows (making a 'double biceps' pose).
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return to the starting position.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you extend your arms.
cues: Pull the rope apart, not just back.
Keep your elbows high and wide throughout the movement.
Show off your biceps at the end of each rep.
mistakes: Pulling the rope down toward the chest instead of the face.
Using too much weight, leading to leaning back or using momentum.
Failing to externally rotate the shoulders at the end of the movement.

name: Single-Arm Landmine Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Upper Pectorals, Triceps, Core
setup: Place one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment (or secure it in a corner).
Stand facing the landmine with your feet shoulder-width apart (or in a staggered stance).
Clean the weighted end of the barbell up to shoulder height with one hand.
Hold the end of the sleeve close to your shoulder, keeping your elbow tucked.
Brace your core and lean slightly forward into the barbell.
execution: Press the barbell upward and forward in a diagonal path until your arm is fully extended.
Reach forward slightly at the top of the movement to engage the serratus anterior.
Pause briefly at the top of the press.
Slowly lower the barbell back to your shoulder under control.
Exhale as you press, and inhale as you lower the weight.
cues: Lean into the bar slightly as you press.
Keep your elbow tucked; do not let it flare out to the side.
Keep your hips and shoulders square to the front.
mistakes: Twisting the torso to assist the press instead of keeping the core stable.
Standing too far back, causing the press angle to be too horizontal.
Allowing the elbow to flare out, placing stress on the shoulder joint.

name: Pec Dec Rear Delt Fly
setup: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at shoulder level when you sit.
Sit facing the machine pad (chest against the pad).
Grip the handles with either a neutral (palms facing) or pronated (palms down) grip.
Keep your chest pressed firmly against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Pull your arms back in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue the movement until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Pause and squeeze your rear delts at the peak of the contraction.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position, resisting the weight.
Exhale as you pull back, and inhale as you return.
cues: Keep your chest glued to the pad throughout the movement.
Lead with the back of your shoulders, not your hands.
Keep your shoulders down; do not shrug.
mistakes: Allowing the chest to lift off the pad, which recruits the lower back.
Bending and straightening the elbows, turning the fly into a tricep extension.
Shrugging the shoulders up, shifting the focus to the upper traps.

name: Dumbbell Shrugs
setup: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs (neutral grip).
Keep your arms fully extended and your chest up.
Maintain a neutral spine and look straight ahead.
execution: Elevate your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
Hold the contraction at the top for a full second.
Slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position, feeling a stretch in your traps.
Avoid rolling your shoulders forward or backward during the movement.
Exhale as you shrug up, and inhale as you lower the weights.
cues: Try to touch your shoulders to your ears.
Move your shoulders straight up and down, not in a circle.
Keep your arms straight; do not pull with your biceps.
mistakes: Rolling the shoulders, which places unnecessary stress on the rotator cuffs.
Bending the elbows to help lift the weight.
Jutting the head forward during the shrug, straining the neck.

name: Lu Raises
target: Lateral Deltoids, Upper Trapezius, Rotator Cuff
setup: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding light dumbbells or weight plates.
Hold the weights in front of your thighs with your palms facing forward.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core braced.
Maintain a very slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Raise the weights out to the sides in a wide arc, similar to a lateral raise.
Continue raising the weights past shoulder height, all the way overhead until they almost touch.
As you pass shoulder height, allow your shoulder blades to upwardly rotate naturally.
Slowly reverse the movement, lowering the weights back to your thighs under strict control.
Exhale as you raise the weights overhead, and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Draw a massive circle with the weights.
Keep your palms facing forward or slightly upward throughout the lift.
Control the descent; do not let gravity pull your arms down.
mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy, which compromises form and safety.
Restricting the natural movement of the shoulder blades.
Using excessive momentum or swinging the hips.

name: Incline Bench Dumbbell Y-Raise
target: Lower Trapezius, Posterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids
setup: Set an incline bench to a 30 to 45-degree angle.
Lie chest-down on the bench with your head clearing the top of the pad.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down.
Point your thumbs up toward the ceiling (neutral/supinated grip).
execution: Raise your arms diagonally forward and outward to form a 'Y' shape with your body.
Keep your arms straight and raise them until they are in line with your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
Exhale as you raise your arms, and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Lead with your thumbs toward the ceiling.
Think about reaching long, not just lifting up.
Keep your neck relaxed and neutral.
mistakes: Lifting the arms straight forward (forming an 'I' instead of a 'Y').
Using too much weight, which recruits the upper traps and neck.
Lifting the chest off the bench to complete the movement.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Triceps, Core
setup: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a single dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height.
Position your elbow slightly forward (in the scapular plane) and your palm facing inward or forward.
Place your non-working hand on your hip or out to the side for balance.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to create a stable base.
execution: Press the dumbbell vertically overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Keep your torso completely upright, resisting the urge to lean to the side.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height under control.
Exhale as you press, and inhale as you lower the weight.
cues: Squeeze your abs and glutes to stay upright.
Press straight up, keeping your arm close to your ear at lockout.
Keep your shoulder blade packed down.
mistakes: Leaning the torso to the opposite side to help press the weight.
Allowing the elbow to flare out excessively to the side.
Failing to lock out the arm at the top of the press.

name: Behind the Neck Barbell Press
target: Lateral Deltoids, Anterior Deltoids, Upper Trapezius, Triceps
setup: Set a barbell in a rack at upper-chest height.
Step under the bar, positioning it across your upper traps (like a back squat).
Grip the bar with a wide grip, wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and take a step back, placing your feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and stand tall.
execution: Press the barbell vertically overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your head slightly forward to allow the bar to clear your neck.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back down to your upper traps under strict control.
Exhale as you press, and inhale as you lower the bar.
cues: Keep your core tight to prevent lower back arching.
Control the descent; do not let the bar crash onto your neck.
Press straight up in a vertical line.
mistakes: Performing this exercise with poor shoulder mobility, leading to injury.
Lowering the bar too quickly or too deep, straining the rotator cuff.
Jutting the head excessively forward.

name: Barbell Shrugs
setup: Set a barbell in a rack at mid-thigh height.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Keep your arms fully extended and your chest up.
execution: Elevate your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
Hold the contraction at the top for a full second.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, feeling a stretch in your traps.
Keep your arms straight throughout the entire movement.
Exhale as you shrug, and inhale as you lower the bar.
cues: Shrug straight up and down; do not roll your shoulders.
Keep your elbows locked; let your traps do all the work.
Keep your chin tucked slightly to protect your neck.
mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in a circle, which can cause shoulder impingement.
Bending the elbows to help lift the weight.
Using too much weight, resulting in a very limited range of motion.

name: Dumbbell Incline Y-Raise
target: Lower Trapezius, Posterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids
setup: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Lie chest-down on the bench, securing your feet on the floor.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down.
Rotate your wrists so your thumbs are pointing up and slightly outward.
execution: Raise your arms diagonally forward and outward to form a 'Y' shape.
Keep your arms straight and raise them until they are in line with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
Exhale as you raise the weights, and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Lead with your thumbs.
Keep your neck relaxed and neutral.
Focus on squeezing your lower shoulder blades.
mistakes: Lifting the arms straight forward instead of in a 'Y' angle.
Using too much weight, which causes the upper traps to take over.
Lifting the chest off the bench.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing your legs (pronated grip).
Keep your back flat and your core braced.
execution: Row the dumbbells upward by flaring your elbows out to the sides at a 90-degree angle.
Pull until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Exhale as you row, and inhale as you lower the weights.
cues: Flare your elbows out wide.
Pull with the back of your shoulders.
Keep your neck neutral.
mistakes: Tucking the elbows close to the body, turning it into a lat row.
Rounding the lower back.
Using momentum to jerk the weights up.

name: Kettlebell Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Triceps, Core
setup: Clean a kettlebell to the rack position (resting in the crook of your elbow against your chest).
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Keep your wrist straight and your forearm vertical.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
execution: Press the kettlebell vertically overhead, rotating your arm so your palm faces forward at lockout.
Keep your core tight and avoid leaning backward.
Lock out your elbow at the top of the movement.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position under control.
Exhale as you press, and inhale as you lower the kettlebell.
cues: Keep your wrist completely straight.
Press in a straight line close to your ear.
Squeeze your glutes to protect your back.
mistakes: Allowing the wrist to bend backward.
Leaning to the side or backward during the press.
Failing to lock out the elbow.

name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Raise
setup: Lie flat on your stomach on an elevated flat bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down.
Keep your palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides in a wide arc.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and lead the movement with them.
Raise the weights until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
Exhale as you raise the weights, and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Lead with your elbows.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders.
Keep your neck relaxed.
mistakes: Using too much weight, leading to swinging.
Bending the elbows too much, reducing the lever arm.
Shrugging the shoulders up.

name: Cable Front Raise with Rope
setup: Set a cable pulley to the lowest setting.
Attach a rope handle to the pulley.
Stand facing away from the machine, with the cable running between your legs.
Grip the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and core braced.
execution: Raise your arms forward and upward in a controlled arc.
Continue lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top to feel the contraction in your front delts.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position under control.
Exhale as you raise your arms, and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Keep your torso still; do not swing.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Control the descent.
mistakes: Using momentum to lift the weight.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug up.
Letting the weight stack slam.

name: Single-Arm Cable Rear Delt Fly
setup: Set a cable pulley to shoulder height.
Stand sideways to the machine.
Reach across your body and grab the cable (or D-handle) with your outer hand.
Keep your feet shoulder-width apart and your core braced.
execution: Pull your arm across your body and out to the side in a horizontal arc.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow and your arm parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your rear delt at the end of the movement.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position under control.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return.
cues: Lead with the back of your hand.
Keep your shoulder down.
Control the weight.
mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbow.
Shrugging the shoulder.
Using too much weight.

name: Dumbbell Cubans
target: Rotator Cuff, Posterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids
setup: Stand tall holding light dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Grip the dumbbells with an overhand grip.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back and down.
execution: Perform an upright row, pulling your elbows up until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Holding your upper arms still, externally rotate your shoulders to flip the weights up.
Press the dumbbells overhead to full extension.
Reverse the movement: lower to the rotated position, rotate down, and lower the row.
Breathe continuously throughout the multi-step movement.
cues: Keep your upper arms parallel to the floor during rotation.
Perform each step distinctly.
Use very light weights.
mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy, risking rotator cuff injury.
Rushing the movement and losing control.
Allowing the elbows to drop during rotation.

name: Plate Halos
target: Rotator Cuff, Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Core
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a weight plate by its sides in front of your chest.
Keep your elbows tucked and your core braced.
execution: Begin circling the plate around your head, passing it close to your ear.
Continue the circle behind your head, keeping it low.
Bring the plate around the other side back to your chest.
Alternate directions for each rep.
Inhale as you start, and exhale as you return.
cues: Keep the plate close to your head.
Keep your core tight.
Do not move your head.
mistakes: Moving your head to avoid the plate.
Arching your lower back.
Using too heavy of a plate.

name: Dumbbell Push Press
target: Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids, Triceps, Quadriceps
setup: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Keep your palms facing each other (neutral grip) and elbows tucked.
Brace your core.
execution: Perform a quick, shallow dip by bending your knees slightly.
Explosively drive through your legs to propel the dumbbells upward.
Extend your arms to lock out the dumbbells overhead.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders, absorbing the impact with your knees.
Inhale before the dip, and exhale at lockout.
cues: Dip straight down.
Drive through your heels.
Punch the weights up.
mistakes: Dipping too deep.
Leaning forward during the dip.
Failing to use leg drive.

name: Cable Upright Row
target: Lateral Deltoids, Upper Trapezius, Biceps Brachii
setup: Set a cable pulley to the lowest setting.
Attach a straight bar or EZ-bar to the pulley.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Stand close to the machine, facing it, with your core braced.
execution: Pull the bar vertically up toward your chest, keeping it close to your body.
Lead with your elbows, keeping them higher than your forearms.
Continue pulling until the bar reaches upper-chest level.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you lower the bar.
cues: Keep the bar close to your body.
Pull with your elbows.
Keep your shoulders down.
mistakes: Using a grip that is too narrow.
Pulling the bar too high.
Using momentum to lift the weight.

name: Dumbbell Incline Front Raise
setup: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Lie chest-down on the bench, securing your feet on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang straight down.
Keep your palms facing each other.
execution: Raise your arms straight forward and upward in a controlled arc.
Continue lifting until your arms are in line with your torso.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Exhale as you lift, and inhale as you lower the weights.
cues: Keep your arms straight.
Lift with your front shoulders.
Control the descent.
mistakes: Using too much weight, causing shrugging.
Lifting the chest off the bench.
Using momentum to swing the weights.

name: Kettlebell High Pull
target: Lateral Deltoids, Upper Trapezius, Posterior Deltoids, Gluteus Maximus
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
Hinge at your hips and grip the kettlebell handle with both hands.
Keep your back flat, chest up, and core braced.
execution: Explosively drive through your hips and knees to pull the kettlebell upward.
As the kettlebell rises, bend your elbows and pull them high and wide.

Guide the kettlebell back down to the floor, hinging at your hips to absorb the weight.

cues: Drive through your hips.
Keep your elbows high.
Keep the kettlebell close.
mistakes: Using only your arms to pull the weight.
Rounding your back during the setup or pull.
Allowing the kettlebell to fly too far away from your body.

name: Barbell Bicep Curl
setup: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up) at shoulder-width.
Pull your shoulders back and down, engaging your core.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and fully extend your arms.
execution: Exhale and curl the barbell upward toward your shoulders by flexing at the elbows.
Keep your upper arms stationary; only your forearms should move.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the movement for a brief second.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control.
cues: Keep your elbows pinned to your ribs.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the lift.
Control the weight on the way down.
mistakes: Swinging the body or using momentum to lift the weight.
Allowing the elbows to flare out or drift forward significantly.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Position your hands in a neutral grip with palms facing each other.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core fully engaged.
Let your arms hang fully extended at your sides.
execution: Exhale and curl the dumbbells upward while maintaining the neutral grip.
Raise the weights until your forearms are nearly vertical.
Pause and squeeze the brachioradialis and biceps at the peak.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
cues: Keep your palms facing each other throughout.
Do not let your elbows drift forward.
Lower the weights slowly to maximize tension.
mistakes: Using hip swing or momentum to initiate the curl.
Failing to fully extend the arms at the bottom of the movement.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
setup: Set an incline bench to an angle of approximately 45 degrees.
Sit back on the bench, keeping your back and head firmly against the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging straight down.
Rotate your palms so they are facing forward (supinated grip).
execution: Keep your elbows pinned back and curl the dumbbells upward.
Contract your biceps strongly as the dumbbells approach shoulder height.
Hold the peak contraction for a brief second.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, feeling the stretch.
cues: Keep your elbows pointing straight down at the floor.
Do not let your shoulders roll forward off the bench.
Focus on stretching the biceps at the bottom.
mistakes: Swinging the elbows forward to make the lift easier.
Lifting the upper back and shoulders off the incline pad.

name: Preacher Curl
setup: Adjust the preacher bench height so your armpits rest comfortably on top of the pad.
Sit or stand behind the bench and rest your upper arms flat against the sloping pad.
Grasp an EZ-bar or barbell with an underhand grip.
Ensure your wrists are straight and aligned with your forearms.
execution: Squeeze your biceps and curl the bar upward toward your chin.
Keep your upper arms and chest firmly pressed against the pad.
Pause and squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the bar until your arms are almost fully extended.
cues: Keep your armpits locked tight against the top of the pad.
Do not fully lock out your elbows at the bottom to protect the joints.
Focus on pulling with your biceps, not your wrists.
mistakes: Hyperextending or aggressively locking out the elbows at the bottom.
Lifting the torso or armpits off the pad to leverage the weight.

name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
setup: Attach a straight bar or rope attachment to a high pulley station.
Stand facing the pulley with feet shoulder-width apart and a slight forward lean.
Grasp the attachment with an overhand grip at chest height.
Tuck your elbows close to your sides and engage your core.
execution: Push the bar or rope downward by extending your elbows.
Continue until your arms are fully locked out at the bottom.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return the attachment back to chest height, maintaining control.
cues: Keep your elbows pinned to your ribs like they are on a hinge.
Push through the heels of your hands.
Maintain a stable, slightly forward-leaning torso.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare outward away from the body.
Using body weight to push the cable down instead of isolating the triceps.

name: Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
setup: Sit on a bench with back support or stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Hold a single heavy dumbbell with both hands, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers.
Press the dumbbell directly overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your head facing forward and your core braced.
execution: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending at the elbows.
Lower the weight until your forearms go past parallel to the floor.
Exhale and press the dumbbell back up to the starting overhead position.
Squeeze your triceps at the top of the movement.
cues: Keep your elbows pointing forward, not flaring out to the sides.
Lower the weight slowly to feel a deep stretch in the triceps.
Keep your lower back flat and avoid excessive arching.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare excessively outward.
Arching the lower back excessively to assist with the lift.

name: Skull Crushers
setup: Lie flat on a bench holding an EZ-bar or barbell with an overhand grip.
Extend your arms straight up over your chest, perpendicular to the floor.
Slightly angle your arms back toward your head (about 10-15 degrees).
Plant your feet firmly on the floor and engage your core.
execution: Inhale and lower the bar by bending only at the elbows.
Bring the bar down toward your forehead or just behind your head.
Exhale and push the bar back up to the starting angled position.

cues: Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing straight ahead.
Maintain the slight backward angle of your upper arms throughout.

mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare out to the sides.

name: Parallel Bar Dips
target: Triceps Brachii, Anterior Deltoids, Pectoralis Major
setup: Grab the parallel bars and press yourself up to the starting position.
Lock out your elbows and keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Cross your ankles behind you and bend your knees slightly.
