execution: Inhale and slowly lower your body by bending your elbows.
Lower yourself until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Exhale and push through your palms to return to the starting position.
Squeeze your triceps at the top of the movement.
cues: Keep your elbows tucked close to your body.
Keep your shoulders packed down; do not let them shrug up.
Maintain an upright torso to target the triceps over the chest.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out wide, which strains the shoulder joints.
Dropping down too fast or going too deep, risking shoulder injury.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
target: Triceps Brachii, Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids
setup: Lie flat on a bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands spaced about shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and hold it directly over your chest with locked arms.
Retract your shoulder blades and brace your core.
execution: Inhale and slowly lower the bar to your lower chest or upper abdomen.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides (about 30-45 degrees from your body).
Touch the bar lightly to your chest without bouncing it.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position, locking out your elbows.
cues: Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Push the bar up in a straight line.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the top of the lift.
mistakes: Placing hands too close together (less than 6 inches), which strains the wrists.
Bouncing the bar off the chest to gain momentum.

name: Concentration Curl
setup: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with your feet wide apart.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and lean your torso forward slightly.
Place the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh on the same side.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down with your palm facing away from your leg.
execution: Exhale and curl the dumbbell upward toward your face by flexing your elbow.
Keep your upper arm locked in place against your inner thigh.
Squeeze your bicep hard at the peak of the contraction.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
cues: Keep your upper arm completely stationary against your thigh.
Focus on rotating your pinky finger upward at the top of the curl.
Do not use your torso to swing the weight up.
mistakes: Resting the elbow on top of the thigh instead of the back of the arm against the inside of the thigh.
Using shoulder movement or torso swinging to lift the weight.

name: Cable Bicep Curl
setup: Attach a straight bar or EZ-bar to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up).
Step back slightly to create tension on the cable, keeping your arms extended.
execution: Exhale and curl the bar upward toward your shoulders.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
cues: Keep constant tension on the cable throughout the movement.
Keep your shoulders pinned back and down.
Do not let your elbows flare out.
mistakes: Letting the weight stack slam down between repetitions.
Leaning backward to help pull the cable upward.

name: Reverse Barbell Curl
setup: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder-width.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back.
execution: Exhale and curl the barbell upward toward your shoulders.
Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms throughout.
Squeeze your forearms and biceps at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
cues: Keep your palms facing down throughout the entire lift.
Do not let your wrists bend or sag at the bottom.
Control the descent to maximize forearm engagement.
mistakes: Allowing the wrists to flex or extension to fail under load.
Using momentum or swinging the hips to lift the bar.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
setup: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists hanging over your knees.
Keep your chest slightly forward and shoulders relaxed.
Allow the dumbbells to roll down to your fingertips.
execution: Exhale and curl your wrists upward, lifting the dumbbells as high as possible.
Keep your forearms pressed firmly against your thighs.
Squeeze your forearm flexors at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down, letting them roll to your fingertips.
cues: Only move your wrists; keep your forearms flat on your thighs.
Let the weight roll down to your fingertips for a full range of motion.
Squeeze hard at the top of the curl.
mistakes: Lifting the forearms off the thighs to assist with the curl.
Using a weight that is too heavy, leading to jerky movements.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
setup: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists hanging over your knees.
Keep your chest slightly forward and shoulders relaxed.
Ensure your palms are facing down toward the floor.
execution: Exhale and extend your wrists upward, lifting the dumbbells as high as possible.
Keep your forearms pressed firmly against your thighs.
Squeeze your forearm extensors at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
cues: Keep your forearms glued to your thighs.
Focus on lifting with the back of your hands.
Control the descent; do not let the weights drop quickly.
mistakes: Lifting the elbows or forearms off the thighs.
Using a range of motion that is too short.

name: Dumbbell Kickbacks
setup: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench for support.
Keep your back flat and parallel to the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your opposite hand with a neutral grip.
Pull your elbow up so your upper arm is parallel to your torso.
execution: Exhale and extend your arm straight back by contracting your triceps.
Keep your upper arm completely stationary; only move your forearm.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return the dumbbell to the starting position.
cues: Keep your elbow pinned high and tight to your side.
Do not let your upper arm drop during the movement.
Squeeze and pause at the top of the extension.
mistakes: Swinging the dumbbell back and forth using shoulder momentum.
Allowing the elbow to drop below the torso level.

name: Cable Overhead Triceps Extension
setup: Attach a rope to a high or medium pulley station.
Grasp the rope and turn your body away from the machine.
Step forward into a staggered stance and lean your torso forward slightly.
Bring your hands behind your head with your elbows bent and pointing forward.
execution: Exhale and extend your arms forward and upward in an arc.
Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing forward throughout.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the point of full extension.
Inhale and slowly lower the rope back behind your head.
cues: Keep your elbows pointing forward, not flaring out.
Maintain a stable, braced core to prevent lower back arching.
Extend fully and flare the rope apart at the end of the movement.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare out wide to the sides.
Using a jerky motion or moving the torso to help move the weight.

name: Spider Curl
setup: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Lie prone (face down) with your chest resting against the incline pad.
Grasp an EZ-bar or barbell with an underhand grip.
Let your arms hang straight down perpendicular to the floor.
execution: Exhale and curl the bar upward toward your forehead.
Keep your upper arms stationary and perpendicular to the floor.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
cues: Keep your upper arms pointing straight down at the floor.
Do not let your elbows swing forward as you curl.
Squeeze your biceps at the peak of the movement.
mistakes: Allowing the upper arms to swing forward, which engages the shoulders.
Lifting the chest off the bench pad to complete the lift.

name: Zottman Curl
setup: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Start with your arms fully extended and palms facing forward (supinated).
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged.
Tuck your elbows close to your sides.
execution: Exhale and curl the dumbbells upward while keeping your palms facing up.
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrists so your palms face down (pronated).
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down with the palms-down grip.
At the bottom, rotate your wrists back to the starting palms-up position.
cues: Curl up with palms up, lower down with palms down.
Keep the rotation smooth and controlled at the top.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout.
mistakes: Rotating the wrists too early before reaching the top of the curl.
Dropping the weights too quickly during the negative phase.

name: Single-Arm Cable Triceps Pushdown
setup: Attach a single handle to a high pulley station.
Stand facing the machine and grasp the handle with an overhand or underhand grip.
Tuck your elbow close to your side and step back slightly.
Brace your core and maintain a slight forward lean.
execution: Exhale and push the handle downward by extending your elbow.
Keep your upper arm completely stationary against your side.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the bottom of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return the handle to the starting position.
cues: Keep your elbow locked in place against your ribs.
Focus on isolating the triceps of the working arm.
Control the weight on the way back up.
mistakes: Allowing the elbow to drift forward or outward during the lift.
Using shoulder rotation or body weight to push the cable down.

name: Chin-Ups
setup: Grasp a pull-up bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you).
Space your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang fully with your arms straight and feet off the floor.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down.
execution: Exhale and pull your body upward by flexing your elbows and contracting your lats.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you pull yourself up.
Continue pulling until your chin clears the bar.
Inhale and slowly lower your body back to the starting dead-hang position.
cues: Drive your elbows down toward your ribs.
Keep your core tight and avoid swinging your legs.
Focus on pulling with your biceps and back.
mistakes: Using kicking or kipping motions to get over the bar.
Failing to go through a full range of motion (not lowering all the way down).

name: Bench Dips
setup: Sit on the edge of a flat bench and place your hands next to your hips.
Extend your legs out in front of you with your heels on the floor.
Slide your glutes off the bench, supporting your weight with your arms.
Keep your shoulders packed down and chest proud.
execution: Inhale and lower your hips by bending your elbows.
Lower yourself until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Keep your back close to the edge of the bench throughout.
Exhale and press through your palms to return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your back scraping the bench as you descend.
Do not let your shoulders shrug up toward your ears.
Squeeze your triceps at the top of the movement.
mistakes: Drifting too far forward away from the bench, which strains the shoulders.
Flaring the elbows out wide instead of keeping them pointing backward.

name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
setup: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Position your hands in a neutral grip with palms facing each other.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged.
Let your arms hang fully extended at your sides.
execution: Exhale and curl one dumbbell across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep the palm facing your body throughout the movement.
Squeeze your brachioradialis and bicep at the top of the curl.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, then repeat on the other side.
cues: Curl the weight across your chest, not straight up.
Keep your torso stationary; do not twist your body.
Control the descent of the dumbbell.
mistakes: Twisting the torso to help lift the weight across the body.
Allowing the elbow to flare out away from the body.

name: Cable Hammer Curl with Rope
setup: Attach a rope to the low pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Step back slightly to create tension on the cable, keeping your arms extended.
execution: Exhale and curl your hands upward toward your shoulders.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and stationary.
Squeeze your forearms and biceps at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the rope back to the starting position under control.
cues: Keep your palms facing each other throughout the entire movement.
Keep your elbows pinned to your ribs.
Do not let the weight stack slam at the bottom.
mistakes: Using hip swing or momentum to pull the cable up.
Allowing the elbows to drift forward significantly during the curl.

name: Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
setup: Stand tall and hold a barbell behind your thighs with an overhand grip (palms facing away from your body).
Space your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your feet shoulder-width apart and your core engaged.
Let the barbell hang at arm's length.
execution: Exhale and curl your wrists upward, lifting the barbell as high as possible.
Squeeze your forearm flexors at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Allow the bar to roll down to your fingertips at the bottom for a full stretch.
cues: Only move your wrists; keep your arms straight.
Squeeze your forearms hard at the top of the curl.
Control the descent and feel the stretch in your forearms.
mistakes: Bending the elbows to help lift the weight.
Using a weight that is too heavy, which limits the range of motion.

name: Overhead Cable Curl
setup: Set two high pulleys on a cable crossover machine to a height slightly above your shoulders.
Attach a single D-handle to each pulley.
Stand in the center of the machine and grab each handle with an underhand grip (palms up).
Extend your arms out to the sides parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
execution: Keep your upper arms completely stationary and parallel to the floor.
Exhale and curl your hands inward toward your ears by flexing your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the peak of the contraction.
Inhale and slowly return your hands back to the starting position, maintaining control.
cues: Imagine you are showing off your double-bicep pose.
Keep your elbows high and aligned with your shoulders.
Only move your forearms; keep your upper body completely still.
mistakes: Dropping the elbows down during the curl.
Using too much weight, causing the shoulders to shrug or roll forward.
Not fully extending the arms at the end of each repetition.

name: Tricep Rope Pushdown
setup: Attach a rope attachment to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet hip-width apart and a slight forward lean from the hips.
Grasp the rope handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Pull your elbows down to your sides, bending them at a 90-degree angle.
execution: Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and stationary.
Exhale and push the rope down by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straight.
At the bottom of the movement, flare the ends of the rope outward to maximize tricep contraction.
Inhale and slowly return the rope back to the starting 90-degree angle.
cues: Keep your elbows pinned to your ribs.
Split the rope at the bottom of the movement.
Control the weight on the way up; do not let it pull you forward.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare out or move forward and backward.
Using body weight to push the cable down instead of isolating the triceps.
Failing to fully lock out the elbows at the bottom.

name: Overhead Dumbbell Tricep Extension
setup: Sit on a bench with back support or stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a single dumbbell with both hands, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers under the inner plate.
Lift the dumbbell directly overhead, extending your arms fully.
Keep your core tight and your chest up.
execution: Keep your upper arms close to your head and perpendicular to the floor.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending only at the elbows.
Lower the weight until your forearms touch your biceps or you feel a deep stretch in your triceps.
Exhale and press the dumbbell back up to the starting position by extending your elbows.
cues: Keep your elbows pointing forward, not flaring out to the sides.
Lower the weight slowly to protect your neck and head.
Lock out your elbows at the top and squeeze your triceps.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows excessively outward, which stresses the shoulder joints.
Arching the lower back too much to assist with the lift.
Not using a full range of motion at the bottom.

name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
setup: Attach a rope to a low or mid-height pulley on a cable machine.
Grasp the rope and turn your body away from the machine, bringing the rope overhead.
Step forward to create tension on the cable and assume a staggered stance for stability.
Lean your torso forward slightly and keep your core tight.
execution: Start with your elbows bent and hands behind your head, feeling a stretch in your triceps.
Keep your upper arms stationary and aligned with your torso.
Exhale and extend your arms forward and upward by straightening your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at the peak of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your elbows tucked in close to your ears.
Press the rope away from your head, not straight up.
Maintain a strong, stable core to prevent arching your back.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out wide during the extension.
Using a jerky motion or momentum to move the weight.
Arching the lower back excessively due to poor core engagement.

name: Single-Arm Cable Tricep Pushdown
setup: Attach a single D-handle or use the bare cable on a high pulley.
Stand facing the machine with your feet hip-width apart.
Grasp the handle with an overhand or underhand grip (depending on variation).
Position your elbow close to your side, bent at a 90-degree angle.
execution: Keep your upper arm stationary and your elbow tucked into your side.
Exhale and push the cable down by extending your elbow until your arm is fully straight.
Squeeze your tricep hard at the bottom of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return the handle back to the starting 90-degree angle.
cues: Keep your shoulder down and do not let it shrug.
Focus on isolating the tricep of the working arm.
Control the weight on the eccentric (upward) phase.
mistakes: Allowing the elbow to drift away from the body.
Using the shoulder or upper body to press the weight down.
Not fully locking out the arm at the bottom.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
setup: Sit on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing down).
Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over your knees.
Keep your chest slightly forward and shoulders relaxed.
execution: Inhale and lower the dumbbells as far as possible by bending only at your wrists.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells upward by extending your wrists as high as they can go.
Squeeze your forearm extensors at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
cues: Keep your forearms glued to your thighs.
Focus on lifting with the back of your hands.
Move slowly and avoid jerky motions.
mistakes: Lifting the forearms off the thighs to assist the lift.
Using too much weight, which can strain the wrist joints.
Rushing through the reps without a full range of motion.

name: Plate Pinch
setup: Select two smooth-sided weight plates of equal weight.
Place them together so the smooth sides face outward.
Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Place the plates on the floor or a bench next to you.
execution: Pinch the plates together using only your fingers and thumb of one hand.
Lift the plates off the floor and hold them at your side at arm's length.
Keep your shoulders back, core engaged, and posture upright.
Hold the plates for a set period of time (e.g., 30-60 seconds) before lowering them back down.
cues: Squeeze the plates together as hard as possible.
Keep your arm straight and shoulder packed.
Maintain a tall, upright posture throughout the hold.
mistakes: Using the palm of the hand to support the plates instead of just the fingers.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug or roll forward.
Holding your breath during the exercise.

name: Tate Press
setup: Lie flat on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Extend your arms straight up over your chest with your palms facing your feet.
Position the dumbbells so they are touching or very close together.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor and engage your core.
execution: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells inward and downward toward your chest.
Keep your elbows flaring outward as you lower the weights.
Touch the dumbbells lightly to your chest, keeping your elbows pointed out.
Exhale and press the dumbbells back up to the starting position by extending your elbows.
cues: Keep your elbows pointing out to the sides throughout the movement.
Focus on using your triceps to press the weights back up.
Keep the dumbbells close together but do not let them crash.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to tuck in, turning the exercise into a standard dumbbell press.
Lowering the weights too quickly, risking injury to the chest or face.
Using too heavy of a weight, which can strain the elbow joints.

name: Forearm Plank
setup: Place your forearms on the floor, parallel to each other, with elbows directly under your shoulders.
Extend your legs straight behind you, resting your weight on your toes.
Align your head, neck, and spine in a neutral position, looking down at the floor.
Engage your core, glutes, and quads to establish a rigid, straight line from head to heels.
execution: Hold this rigid position, maintaining a continuous contraction throughout your entire midsection.
Breathe deeply and rhythmically, avoiding holding your breath.
Keep your shoulders pulled down and away from your ears.
Maintain the hold for the prescribed duration without letting your hips sag or rise.
cues: Squeeze your glutes and pull your belly button toward your spine.
Push the floor away through your elbows to active your upper back.
Imagine a straight rod running from your head to your heels.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch and the hips to sag toward the floor.
Piking the hips up into the air, shifting the load away from the core.
Holding your breath instead of maintaining steady, controlled breathing.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
target: Rectus Abdominis, Transverse Abdominis, Latissimus Dorsi
setup: Kneel on a soft mat or pad with your knees hip-width apart.
Grasp the handles of the ab wheel with both hands, placing it on the floor directly beneath your shoulders.
Engage your core, tuck your pelvis slightly (posterior pelvic tilt), and round your upper back slightly.
Keep your arms straight but not locked out.
execution: Slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your hips and arms simultaneously.
Lower your torso toward the floor in a controlled manner, going only as far as you can maintain a flat or slightly rounded lower back.
Pause for a brief second at the point of maximum extension.
Contract your abs to pull the wheel back toward your knees, returning to the starting position.
cues: Roll out with your hips, not just your arms.
Keep your tailbone tucked and do not let your lower back arch.
Pull back using your stomach muscles, not your hips or arms.
mistakes: Arching the lower back and letting the hips sag, which transfers the load to the lumbar spine.
Initiating the return movement by pushing the hips back first instead of contracting the abs.
Bending the elbows during the movement, turning it into an arm exercise.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip (palms facing away), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Allow your legs to hang straight down, keeping your feet together.
Engage your shoulders by pulling them down away from your ears (active shoulders).
Brace your core to minimize any initial body swinging.
execution: Exhale and slowly bend your knees, drawing them up toward your chest.
Tilt your pelvis upward at the top of the movement to fully contract your abdominal muscles.
Pause for a brief second at the peak of the contraction.
Inhale and slowly lower your knees back to the starting position with control.
cues: Pull your knees to your chest, not just your thighs to your hips.
Keep your shoulders active and do not swing your body.
Control the descent; do not let your legs drop passively.
mistakes: Using momentum and swinging the legs to get them up.
Keeping the shoulders passive and hanging completely relaxed, which strains the shoulder joints.
Failing to tilt the pelvis at the top, resulting in a hip-flexor-dominant movement.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width, overhand grip.
Keep your legs fully extended and squeezed together.
Depress your shoulder blades to engage your lats and stabilize your upper body.
Brace your core to prevent your torso from swinging.
execution: Keeping your legs straight, exhale and raise them upward by flexing at the hips.
Continue raising your legs until they are parallel to the floor or higher, tilting your pelvis backward.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement to maximize abdominal tension.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, resisting gravity all the way down.
cues: Keep your legs perfectly straight and squeezed together.
Imagine folding your body in half at the waist.
Control the down phase to eliminate swinging.
mistakes: Swinging the legs and using momentum to complete the repetition.
Bending the knees significantly, which reduces the lever arm and difficulty.
Allowing the lower back to arch excessively at the bottom of the movement.

name: Cable Woodchopper
setup: Position a cable pulley at the high setting and attach a standard D-handle.
Stand sideways to the cable machine, about arm's length away, with feet wider than shoulder-width.
Grasp the handle with both hands, extending your arms fully toward the pulley.
Rotate your torso toward the machine, keeping your hips facing forward.
execution: In one continuous motion, pull the cable diagonally downward and across your body toward your opposite knee.
Rotate your torso and pivot your back foot as you pull, keeping your arms straight.
Pause briefly at the end of the movement, squeezing your obliques.
Slowly return to the starting position under control, resisting the pull of the cable.
cues: Rotate from your torso, not just your arms.
Pivot on your back foot like you are throwing a punch.
Keep your arms long and locked out throughout the movement.
mistakes: Bending the elbows and pulling with the arms instead of rotating the torso.
Keeping the feet glued to the floor, which places excessive twisting stress on the knees.
Moving too quickly and using momentum rather than controlled muscular contraction.

name: Russian Twist
setup: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Lean your torso back at a 45-degree angle, keeping your spine straight and chest open.
Clasp your hands together in front of your chest (or hold a weight/medicine ball).
Optionally, lift your feet a few inches off the floor to balance on your sit bones.
execution: Slowly rotate your torso to the right, bringing your hands or weight toward the floor beside your hip.
Pause briefly, feeling the contraction in your left oblique.
Rotate your torso back through the center and over to the left side.
Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled manner.
cues: Rotate your shoulders, not just your hands.
Keep your chest proud and avoid rounding your spine.
Keep your knees as still as possible as you twist.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back, which increases spinal shear stress.
Moving only the arms back and forth without actually rotating the ribcage.
Moving too fast, which relies on momentum rather than core control.

name: Deadbug
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms extended straight up toward the ceiling.
Raise your legs so your knees are bent at a 90-degree angle (thighs vertical, shins parallel to the floor).
Flatten your lower back completely against the floor, leaving no gap.
Brace your core as if preparing to be punched in the stomach.
execution: Slowly lower your right arm overhead while simultaneously extending your left leg straight out.
Lower both limbs until they are just a few inches off the floor, keeping your lower back glued to the mat.
Pause for a moment in the extended position.
Return your arm and leg to the starting position, then repeat with the left arm and right leg.
cues: Squish an imaginary grape under your lower back.
Move slowly and with absolute control.
Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch off the floor during extension.
Moving the limbs too quickly, losing the bracing element.
Moving the resting arm or leg while the opposite limbs are extending.

name: Bird Dog
target: Erector Spinae, Gluteus Maximus, Rectus Abdominis
setup: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position on a mat.
Place your hands directly under your shoulders and knees directly under your hips.
Maintain a neutral spine, looking down at the floor slightly ahead of your hands.
Engage your core to stabilize your pelvis and torso.
execution: Slowly extend your right arm straight forward and your left leg straight backward.
Reach until both limbs are parallel to the floor, forming a straight line from hand to foot.
Hold this position for 1-2 seconds, focusing on balance and core stability.
Slowly lower both limbs back to the starting tabletop position and repeat on the opposite side.
cues: Reach forward with your hand and kick backward with your heel.
Keep your hips level; do not let them tilt to the side.
Keep your neck neutral; look at the floor.
mistakes: Arching the lower back excessively by lifting the leg too high.
Allowing the hips to tilt or rotate to one side during extension.
Rushing through the movement instead of holding and stabilizing.

name: Pallof Press
setup: Set a cable pulley to chest height and attach a standard D-handle.
Stand sideways to the machine, pull the handle to the center of your chest, and hold it with both hands.
Step away from the machine to create tension on the cable, standing with feet shoulder-width apart.
Slightly bend your knees, tuck your pelvis, and brace your core.
execution: Slowly press the handle straight out in front of your chest until your arms are fully extended.
Resist the lateral pull of the cable, keeping your hands centered with your sternum.
Hold the extended position for 2 seconds while maintaining a rigid torso.
Slowly bring the handle back to your chest, resisting the tension under control.
cues: Do not let the cable pull or twist your torso.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs as you press.
Keep your shoulders down and back.
mistakes: Allowing the torso to rotate toward the cable machine.
Rushing the press and return phases, reducing time under tension.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears during the press.

name: Dragon Flag
target: Rectus Abdominis, Transverse Abdominis, Hip Flexors
setup: Lie face up on a flat bench, reaching behind your head to firmly grip the edges of the bench near your ears.
Pull your knees up toward your chest and lift your hips off the bench.
Extend your legs straight up toward the ceiling, creating a straight line from your shoulders to your toes.
Support your weight on your upper back and shoulders, not your neck.
execution: Slowly lower your straight body down toward the bench in a controlled arc.
Keep your body perfectly rigid, ensuring only your upper back remains in contact with the bench.
Lower your legs until your body is just hovering above the bench.
Reverse the movement by pulling your body back up to the vertical position using your core.
cues: Keep your body as stiff as a board from shoulders to toes.
Do not let your hips sag or bend at the waist.
Pull with your abs and lats, not just your arms.
mistakes: Bending at the hips, which turns the exercise into a simple leg raise.
Allowing the lower back to arch excessively, placing strain on the lumbar spine.
Dropping the body too quickly instead of controlling the eccentric phase.

name: Bicycle Crunch
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your lower back pressed into the floor.
Place your hands lightly behind your head, keeping your elbows flared out wide.
Lift your shoulder blades off the floor and raise your legs, bending your knees at a 90-degree angle.
execution: Extend your right leg straight out at a 45-degree angle while pulling your left knee toward your chest.
Simultaneously rotate your torso to the left, bringing your right elbow toward your left knee.
Switch sides by extending your left leg, pulling your right knee in, and rotating your left elbow to your right knee.
Continue alternating sides in a smooth, pedaling motion.
cues: Think about bringing your shoulder to your knee, not just your elbow.
Keep your lower back pressed firmly into the floor.
Move with control; do not rush the pedaling motion.
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands, which strains the cervical spine.
Moving too fast and relying on momentum rather than muscle contraction.
Allowing the lower back to arch off the floor during leg extension.

name: Reverse Crunch
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms by your sides, palms facing down.
Raise your legs and bend your knees to a 90-degree angle, keeping your feet together.
Press your lower back flat against the floor and brace your core.
execution: Contract your lower abdominals to curl your hips up and off the floor, pulling your knees toward your chest.
At the top of the movement, reach your feet slightly toward the ceiling.
Pause for a brief second at the peak of the contraction.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the floor, resisting gravity.
cues: Peel your spine off the floor starting from your tailbone.
Use your lower abs to lift, not your hands pushing into the floor.
Control the descent; do not let your hips slam down.
mistakes: Using momentum by swinging the legs back and forth.
Pushing excessively with the hands and arms to force the hips up.
Dropping the hips quickly without controlling the eccentric phase.

name: Toes to Bar
target: Rectus Abdominis, Iliopsoas (Hip Flexors), Latissimus Dorsi
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Engage your shoulders and lats to create a stable, active hang.
Initiate a slight hollow-body position to prepare for the movement.
execution: Pull down on the bar with your arms while simultaneously lifting your legs upward.
Keep your legs as straight as possible as they rise toward the bar.
Touch the bar with both toes simultaneously between your hands.
Lower your legs back down with control, returning to the active hang position.
cues: Push the bar down with your hands as you lift your feet.
Keep your core tight to prevent excessive swinging at the bottom.
Squeeze your quads to keep your legs straight.
mistakes: Using excessive kipping or swinging momentum without core control.
Allowing the shoulders to go completely passive, straining the shoulder joints.
Letting the legs drop rapidly, losing the eccentric phase of the lift.

name: L-Sit
setup: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight out in front of you, feet together.
Place your hands flat on the floor (or on parallettes/blocks) next to your hips.
Depress your shoulders and engage your lats, preparing to lift your body.
execution: Press down firmly through your hands to lift your hips off the floor.
Simultaneously contract your abs and hip flexors to lift your legs parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees locked out and toes pointed, forming an 'L' shape with your body.
Hold this position for the desired duration while maintaining steady breathing.
cues: Push the floor away to keep your shoulders down.
Squeeze your thighs together and lock your knees.
Keep your chest up and avoid excessive rounding of the upper back.
mistakes: Allowing the shoulders to shrug up toward the ears.
Bending the knees because of tight hamstrings or weak hip flexors.
Letting the hips drift backward behind the hands instead of keeping them aligned.

name: Side Plank
setup: Lie on your side on a mat, stacking your feet, knees, and hips on top of each other.
Prop your upper body up on your elbow, placing it directly underneath your shoulder.
Keep your forearm flat on the floor, pointing forward.
Engage your core and prepare to lift your hips.
execution: Lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Extend your top arm straight up toward the ceiling or place it on your hip.
Keep your neck neutral, looking straight ahead.
Hold this position, keeping your hips elevated and core braced.
cues: Push your bottom hip up toward the ceiling.
Keep your shoulder directly over your elbow.
Squeeze your glutes to keep your hips pushed forward.
mistakes: Allowing the hips to sag toward the floor.
Rotating the chest and hips forward instead of keeping them stacked vertically.
Placing the elbow too far forward, straining the shoulder joint.

name: Hollow Body Hold
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight and arms extended overhead.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor, leaving no space between your back and the mat.
Squeeze your legs together and point your toes.
execution: Simultaneously lift your legs, head, shoulders, and upper back off the floor.
Keep your arms extended overhead, parallel to your ears.
Maintain a shallow, banana-like curve with your body, supported only by your lower back and glutes.
Hold this position, breathing shallowly while keeping your core fully braced.
cues: Glue your lower back to the floor.
Squeeze your legs together and reach through your toes.
Keep your chin tucked slightly, looking toward your toes.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch off the floor, which transfers the load to the spine.
Lifting the legs too high, which makes the exercise too easy and reduces core tension.
Holding your breath instead of maintaining controlled, shallow breathing.

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
setup: Step up onto the Captain's Chair station and place your forearms on the padded armrests.
Grip the handles firmly and press your back flat against the padded backrest.
Let your legs hang straight down, keeping your feet together.
Push down through your elbows to keep your shoulders active and away from your ears.
execution: Exhale and slowly raise your legs straight out in front of you until they are parallel to the floor.
Tilt your pelvis upward at the top of the movement to fully engage your abdominals.
Pause for a brief second at the peak of the contraction.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, resisting gravity.
cues: Press your lower back firmly into the pad.
Lift your legs with control; do not swing them.
Keep your shoulders down and chest proud.
mistakes: Using momentum and swinging the legs to complete the lift.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug up, which strains the neck and upper back.
Arching the lower back away from the pad at the bottom of the movement.

name: Cable Crunch
setup: Attach a rope attachment to a high pulley cable machine.
Kneel down facing the machine (or facing away), holding the rope handles next to your ears or temples.
Position your hips high and slightly back, keeping your thighs vertical.
Brace your core and lock your hips in place.
execution: Exhale and flex your spine, drawing your elbows down toward your knees.
Focus on curling your torso, bringing your chest toward your pelvis.
Squeeze your abdominals hard at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, allowing your spine to extend slightly at the top.
cues: Crunch with your abs, not by pulling with your arms.
Keep your hips locked in place; do not sit back onto your heels.
Imagine rolling your spine into a tight ball.
mistakes: Sitting back onto the heels during the crunch, which uses body weight instead of abdominal strength.
Pulling the rope down with the arms and shoulders rather than flexing the spine.
Keeping the spine completely flat, which prevents full abdominal contraction.

name: Medicine Ball Slam
setup: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a non-bouncing medicine ball (slam ball) with both hands.
Keep your spine neutral and your core braced.
Hold the ball at chest height to start.
execution: Inhale and reach the medicine ball high overhead, extending your hips and standing on your toes.
Using your core and lats, aggressively slam the ball down onto the floor directly in front of you.
Follow through with your body, bending your knees and hinging at the hips as you slam.
Catch the ball on the rebound (if any) or pick it up to repeat.
cues: Slam with your core, not just your arms.
Throw the ball through the floor.
Hinge your hips back as you throw.
mistakes: Using only the arms to throw the ball, neglecting the power from the core and hips.
Rounding the lower back excessively when picking up the ball.
Standing too close to the ball's landing spot, risking it bouncing back into the face.

name: Windshield Wipers
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms extended straight out to the sides for stability, palms down.
Raise your legs straight up toward the ceiling so they are perpendicular to the floor.
Squeeze your legs together and flex your feet.
Press your shoulders firmly into the mat.
execution: Slowly lower your legs to the right side, keeping them straight and together.
Lower them as far as possible without letting your left shoulder lift off the floor.
Pause briefly, then use your obliques to pull your legs back to the center.
Repeat the movement to the left side, keeping the descent controlled.
cues: Keep both shoulders glued to the floor.
Control the descent; do not let your legs drop.
Squeeze your legs together like they are one single limb.
mistakes: Allowing the opposite shoulder to lift off the floor, losing the rotational stretch and contraction.
Bending the knees significantly, which reduces the difficulty and core engagement.
Moving too quickly and using momentum to swing the legs side to side.

name: Stability Ball Crunch
setup: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward until your lower back is supported by the curve of the ball.
Place your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, with knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Lean back slightly to stretch your abdominals over the ball.
execution: Exhale and contract your abs to curl your upper torso upward.
Focus on bringing your ribcage toward your pelvis, keeping the ball stable.
Pause at the top of the movement for a brief second.
Inhale and slowly lower your torso back over the ball, getting a deep stretch at the bottom.
cues: Curl your ribs to your hips.
Keep the ball completely still throughout the movement.
Look up at the ceiling to avoid pulling on your neck.
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands, causing strain.
Using the legs to push the ball back and forth instead of using the abs to crunch.
Rushing through the movement and skipping the stretch at the bottom.

name: Turkish Get-Up
target: Obliques, Rectus Abdominis, Deltoids, Gluteus Maximus
setup: Lie on your side next to a kettlebell, grasp it with both hands, and roll onto your back.
Press the kettlebell straight up with your right arm, keeping your elbow locked and shoulder packed.
Bend your right knee, placing your right foot flat on the floor close to your butt.
Extend your left arm and left leg out at a 45-degree angle from your body.
execution: Roll up onto your left forearm, then press up onto your left hand, keeping your eyes on the kettlebell.
Bridge your hips high off the floor, then sweep your left leg back and place your left knee under your hip.
Lift your hand off the floor to align your torso vertically, entering a half-kneeling lunge position.
Stand up completely by pushing through your front heel, bringing your feet together, then reverse the steps to lie down.
cues: Keep your eyes locked on the kettlebell at all times.
Keep the loaded arm perfectly vertical and elbow locked.
Move slowly and treat each step as an individual exercise.
mistakes: Allowing the elbow of the loaded arm to bend, risking loss of control.
Rushing through the transitions, leading to instability and loss of balance.
Failing to pack the shoulder, which places excessive strain on the rotator cuff.

name: Suitcase Carry
setup: Place a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell on the floor next to your foot.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to pick up the weight with one hand, using proper deadlift form.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, shoulders back, and chest proud.
Keep your opposite arm free or lightly clenched in a fist for balance.
execution: Walk forward in a straight line, taking slow, deliberate, and controlled steps.
Maintain a perfectly upright posture, resisting the urge to lean toward or away from the weighted side.
Keep your core braced and shoulders level throughout the walk.
Turn around carefully and walk back, then switch the weight to the opposite hand.
cues: Stand tall and do not let the weight pull you sideways.
Walk as if you have a cup of water balancing on your head.
Keep your shoulders level and square.
mistakes: Leaning to the opposite side to compensate for the weight.
Allowing the weight to rest against the thigh, which reduces core engagement.
Taking fast, rushed steps instead of slow, controlled strides.

name: V-Up
setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight and arms extended overhead.
Keep your feet together and your lower back pressed into the floor.
Engage your core to prepare for the explosive lift.
execution: In one fluid motion, lift your torso and your legs off the floor, reaching your hands toward your feet.
Aim to balance on your sit bones, forming a 'V' shape with your body at the peak.
Pause briefly at the top, squeezing your abdominals.
Slowly lower your arms and legs back to the starting position with control.
cues: Fold your body like a book.
Reach for your toes at the top.
Control the descent; do not just flop back down.
mistakes: Bending the knees significantly, which reduces the lever arm and core demand.
Using excessive momentum and throwing the arms forward without engaging the abs.
Allowing the lower back to slam into the floor during the descent.

name: RKC Plank
target: Rectus Abdominis, Transverse Abdominis, Gluteus Maximus
setup: Assume a standard forearm plank position with your elbows under your shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
Clasp your hands together in front of you.
Lock your knees out completely and squeeze your glutes to create a posterior pelvic tilt.
execution: Actively pull your elbows down toward your toes and pull your toes up toward your elbows.
Do not actually move your limbs; instead, create an intense isometric contraction.
Squeeze your quads, glutes, and abs as hard as possible.
Maintain this maximum tension hold for 10-20 seconds while breathing shallowly.
cues: Pull your elbows to your toes and toes to your elbows.
Squeeze your glutes like you are trying to crack a nut.
Make every muscle in your body as hard as stone.
mistakes: Holding a passive plank instead of actively pulling the elbows and toes together.
Allowing the hips to sag or rise, breaking the straight line.
Holding the breath during the high-tension hold.

name: Plank
setup: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows aligned below shoulders.
Extend your legs straight behind you, resting on your toes.
Keep your feet hip-width apart for stability.
Align your head, neck, and spine in a neutral position.
execution: Engage your core by pulling your belly button toward your spine.
Squeeze your glutes and quadriceps to lock your body in a straight line.
Hold this rigid position while breathing deeply and steadily.
Avoid letting your hips sag or rise throughout the duration.
cues: Pull your elbows toward your toes to increase tension.
Keep your gaze down at the floor.
Imagine a straight line from your head to your heels.
mistakes: Saging hips, which strains the lower back.
Raising the hips too high, reducing core engagement.
Holding your breath instead of breathing steadily.

name: Flutter Kicks
setup: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and arms by your sides.
Place your hands under your glutes for lower back support if needed.
Lift your head, neck, and shoulders slightly off the floor.
Raise your feet about 6 inches off the ground.
execution: Keep your legs straight and toes pointed.
Flutter your legs up and down in a small, rapid motion.
Keep your lower back pressed firmly into the floor.
Continue the kicking motion for the desired duration.
cues: Keep your lower back glued to the floor.
Kick from your hips, not your knees.
Keep your legs long and tight.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch off the floor.
Bending the knees and riding a 'bicycle' instead of kicking.
Lifting the legs too high, reducing core tension.

name: Mountain Climbers
setup: Start in a high plank position with hands under shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your feet hip-width apart.
Distribute your weight evenly between your hands and toes.
execution: Drive your right knee toward your chest with control.
Quickly return your right foot to the starting position.
Immediately drive your left knee toward your chest.
Alternate legs rapidly while maintaining a stable torso.
cues: Keep your hips down and level.
Run on the spot while keeping your upper body still.
Push the floor away with your hands.
mistakes: Bouncing the hips up and down during the movement.
Letting the shoulders drift behind the hands.
Failing to engage the core, causing the lower back to sag.

name: Bear Crawl Hold
setup: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Align your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Tuck your toes and engage your core.
Keep your spine neutral and gaze down.
execution: Press through your hands and toes to lift your knees 1-2 inches.
Hold this hovering position while keeping your back flat.
Keep your core braced and breathe deeply.
Lower your knees back to the floor after the set time.
cues: Hover your knees just barely off the floor.
Keep your back flat like a tabletop.
Push the floor away to engage your shoulders.
mistakes: Lifting the hips too high, turning it into a downward dog.
Letting the knees flare out or sag.
Allowing the lower back to arch.

name: Plank Shoulder Taps
setup: Start in a high plank position with hands under shoulders.
Set your feet slightly wider than hip-width for stability.
Engage your core, glutes, and quadriceps.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
execution: Slowly lift your right hand and tap your left shoulder.
Place your right hand back down with control.
Lift your left hand and tap your right shoulder.
Alternate sides while keeping your hips completely still.
cues: Imagine a glass of water balancing on your lower back.
Squeeze your glutes to lock your hips in place.
Move slowly and minimize body rotation.
mistakes: Shifting or rocking the hips from side to side.
Rushing the taps and losing control.
Letting the hips sag or rise too high.
